📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With declining sales, annual capacity cuts approaching a million units, and a wave of affordable Chinese competitors entering Western markets, Volkswagen is facing down its own mortality. Rather than fighting it, the company is leaning in and announcing plans to export roughly 300,000 Made-in-China VWs per year by 2030.

American dealers won’t be getting any Made-in-China vehicles (not at first, anyway), but for Mexican, South American, Middle Eastern, African, and Southeast Asian markets, the shift to lower-cost Chinese manufacturing marks a major strategic pivot. In addition to exporting budget-friendly sedans like the Jetta VA3, Volkswagen is also considering a move to adopt Xpeng’s tech stack for up to 75% of its core European lineup.

The move comes as Volkswagen’s Chinese JVs face a sharp sales decline in their home market, selling just 1.2 million new cars in the first nine months of 2026 (down 35% compared to last year). The financial story is even worse, with last year’s roughly $815 million profit falling to a more than $120 million loss.

“The sharp decline in the overall market in China remains an industry-wide challenge,” said Martin Sander, Volkswagen Group’s sales boss, before adding that VW’s “newly introduced, locally developed electric models are beginning to make an impact.”.

Sources indicate that add in rising energy costs, continuing software complications, and serious labor disputes with the IG Metall union in Europe, and Volkswagen may not have much choice in the matter – which is why it’s not exactly surprising to see VW consider turning China into an export hub. And that 300,000 number? That may be just the start.

On Volkswagen’s third-quarter results call, CFO Arno Antlitz reportedly called that 300,000 annual export target “conservative,” adding that overseas shipments could help offset the carmaker’s weakening prospects in China.

Driven: 2027 Audi Q7 and SQ7 SUVs Muscle Up

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Over the past two decades, if you were looking for an upscale three-row German SUV, the Audi Q7 or its performance-oriented SQ7 sibling was likely on your shopping list.
  • According to recent reports, the mid-size Audi SUVs are completely new for 2027, but the automaker has been careful not to stray too far from a blueprint that has proved so successful.
  • Industry observers note that while the Q7’s dimensions grow slightly in most directions, it’s still roughly the same size as before, and its three-row layout could best be described as a 5+2, as the cramped rearmost chairs are best used by children and only in a pinch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over the past two decades, if you were looking for an upscale three-row German SUV, the Audi Q7 or its performance-oriented SQ7 sibling was likely on your shopping list. Both have long delivered on style, family-friendliness, and luxury.

According to recent reports, the mid-size Audi SUVs are completely new for 2027, but the automaker has been careful not to stray too far from a blueprint that has proved so successful. With this latest generation, the Q7’s design has been brought up to speed with the rest of the Audi lineup. That means softer edges, a more muscular stance, and a lot more digital displays inside.

Industry observers note that while the Q7’s dimensions grow slightly in most directions, it’s still roughly the same size as before, and its three-row layout could best be described as a 5+2, as the cramped rearmost chairs are best used by children and only in a pinch. If you need more space, there’s now a full-size Q9 model that’s larger inside and out.

See all results for fresh 2027 Audi Q7 for sale near 11743.

Industry observers note that the Q7 does gain a sought-after second-row feature: optional captain’s chairs. Choosing the two-seat second row reduces seat count from seven to six, but it also decreases the risk of sibling quarrels.

Speaking of the cabin, we’ve complained that Audi’s latest interiors haven’t lived up to the standard set by the manufacturer’s earlier efforts, but the new Q7 represents a reversal of that trend. Granted, the models we sampled were well-optioned examples, but the interior materials are premium, and even the $72,295 base model gets genuine leather upholstery and real wood inlays.

Industry observers note that upgrade to a higher Q7 trim, and you’ll enjoy luxuries such as soft-close doors, a Bang & Olufsen stereo, and massaging front seats. The SQ7 comes in just one trim level, starting at $100,095, and it’s comprehensively equipped with only a few available packages, most of them designed to improve performance and handling.

Special attention has been paid to the SUV’s exterior lighting elements. There are a lot of them, and some are genuinely useful, none more so than Audi’s digital matrix headlights.

Recent findings suggest that not only do these high-tech headlamps deliver a shockingly bright view of the road ahead, but they also sense oncoming vehicles and will temporarily deactivate some of their bulbs to avoid blinding other motorists. A set of OLED taillights illuminate in different ways depending on context, with the intent to help communicate with other drivers: For example, if another vehicle is too close to the Q7’s rear bumper in traffic, the lights will illuminate with additional brightness as a warning to back off.

Other flashy features push into gimmick territory. There’s a light-up grille, a customizable taillamp and daytime-running-light signature, and a system that projects arrows on the street surface to indicate which direction the driver is signaling. Are blinkers no longer enough? Luckily, if you don’t want your Audi lighting up like a Christmas tree, some of these features can be deactivated via the Q7’s infotainment system.

See all results for upcoming 2027 Audi Q7 for sale near 11743.

Speaking of infotainment, there are a lot of screens inside the Q7. A large infotainment touchscreen is expected, surely, but there’s also a digital gauge display, a passenger’s display, and an optional head-up display.

While the previous-generation Q7 offered a turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-four as standard with a turbocharged 3.0-liter V-6 as an upgrade, the 2027 model ditches the four-banger altogether, making a V-6 standard. This version’s six—a turbo 2.9-liter—packs 429 horsepower, a 94-hp advantage over the outgoing model.

A twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V-8 has always powered the SQ7, and the newly introduced generation is no different. It also gets more power, jumping from 500 horsepower in 2026 to 591 horsepower in 2027.

According to recent reports, acceleration is plentiful in the Q7, which makes quick work of highway passing maneuvers and will beat most regular traffic off the line with a quick stab of the throttle. Audi estimates a 4.8-second 60-mph time.

Recent findings suggest that the SQ7 is another animal altogether. While both SUVs have launch control, using it in the SQ7 results in a giggle-inducing run to highway speeds. Audi wagers a 60-mph run would take just 3.7 seconds. The V-8’s muted burble is a bonus.

Industry observers note that confident and predictable handling, an Audi touchstone, remains the default. While all Q7s come with Balanced, Dynamic, and Comfort drive modes, those with the optional air-spring suspension benefit most, with each mode delivering noticeably different ride qualities. SQ7s get air springs as standard but can be optioned with a sport-tuned version of the system, which lowers the ride height 1.2 inches in Dynamic mode and firms everything up to the max.

SQ7 models also feature a retuned all-wheel-drive system with more rear bias. Unlike previous Audi performance SUVs, which were short on driving drama, the newly introduced SQ7’s more fun-loving nature shines on twisty roads with that newfound rear-end boogie. Our test drive took us down some of northern California’s twistiest roads, and both SUVs proved entertaining and luxurious.

With this latest generation, Audi has boosted the Q7 and SQ7’s swank factor. It has modernized their styling without introducing a new polarizing design language while adding options buyers want. Retaining the Q7’s just-right size and keeping the focus on refined, performance-oriented road manners is the hedge that will keep it near the top of the shopping list of enthusiast drivers who need family-sized space.

China’s SC01 EV Sports Car Will Get Its Own Factory In Europe

💡 Key Takeaways
  • China’s SC01 electric sports car, which wowed reviewers for its great handling and back-to-basics approach to EVs, is getting its own European factory, with a scheduled production start in May 2027.
  • The two-door EV, which was developed by Tianjin Gongjiangpai Auto Technology (TGAT), will be assembled at a latest facility in central Italy by FIPA Europe, a company that currently makes Chinese microcars.
  • The first phase of the European SC01 program involves a 20,000-square-meter (21,527-square-feet) production space and 50 employees who will work to assemble the electric two-seater from kits shipped from China.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

China’s SC01 electric sports car, which wowed reviewers for its great handling and back-to-basics approach to EVs, is getting its own European factory, with a scheduled production start in May 2027.

The two-door EV, which was developed by Tianjin Gongjiangpai Auto Technology (TGAT), will be assembled at a latest facility in central Italy by FIPA Europe, a company that currently makes Chinese microcars. The importer has signed a contract for an existing industrial complex in the Marche region, and work is expected to begin early next year, according to Electrive.

The first phase of the European SC01 program involves a 20,000-square-meter (21,527-square-feet) production space and 50 employees who will work to assemble the electric two-seater from kits shipped from China. A 2,750-square-meter (29,600 sq ft) warehouse and a 20,000-square-meter (21,5278 sq ft) logistics area are also planned for the new facility.

Recent findings suggest that however, that’s just the start, as FIPA Europe looks to expand the floor space and its headcount by the end of the decade, with 285 jobs expected by the last day of 2030. The company, which assembles the Desner T80, a low-speed electric microcar, claims to be the only authorized importer and manufacturer of the SC01 for the European Union and the only company responsible for the car’s European homologation.

The first SC01 prototypes are reportedly already roaming Italy’s streets, imported from China for development purposes. The next step is to install the assembly lines at the new factory in the first quarter of 2027, with the first Italian-built SC01s scheduled to roll out the door in May.

As a reminder, the Chinese-spec SC01 is powered by a 430-horsepower (320-kilowatt) dual-motor powertrain that draws electricity from a 60-kilowatt-hour battery pack. The car was developed with backing from tech giant Xiaomi and is assembled in China by JMEV, a joint venture between Groupe Renault and Jiangling Motors Corporation Group.

The car’s biggest trait is its low weight. Tipping the scales at less than 1,400 kilograms (3,086 pounds), it’s lighter than a Porsche 911 and can sprint from zero to 62 mph (0-100 kilometers per hour) in 2.9 seconds. What’s more, the car’s dual-motor powertrain can be configured to work either independently or together, so the driver can choose from rear-wheel drive, front-wheel drive, or all-wheel drive.

Inside, there’s just the bare minimum, with a digital instrument cluster and a few physical controls on the center console. There’s no infotainment screen, let alone a passenger display, as is the case with many modern luxury cars nowadays.

Pricing hasn’t been declared for the European version of the SC01, but in China, the back-to-basics EV retails for the equivalent of about $32,000.

It has been revealed that BMW’s upcoming iX4 is almost here, and it could make range anxiety a thing of the past. With 428 miles of EPA range, more than 500 miles on the WLTP cycle, and ultra-fast charging, the new EV could make road trips a whole lot easier.

Series production of the new iX4 is officially underway at BMW Group’s manufacturing plant in Debrecen, Hungary.

The iX4 is the second fully electric BMW model built at the facility, following the record-breaking production ramp-up of the fresh iX3 SUV.

BMW said the plant began series production of an entirely new model in less than two months after the manufacturer introduced a 24-hour, three-shift schedule to ramp up output to meet higher-than-expected demand.

The new iX4 will go on sale in March 2027 as an all-electric replacement for the X4. It will be available in two variants: the BMW iX4 50 xDrive and BMW iX4 40 xDrive, with a range-topping M60 xDrive set to follow shortly after.

Both versions use a dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain. The iX4 50 xDrive provides a combined 468 hp and 475 lb-ft of torque, enabling it to sprint from 0 to 60 mph in 4.7 seconds.

The performance M60 version delivers a combined 603 hp and 645 lb-ft of torque, which BMW claims is good for a 0 to 60 mph sprint in just 3.9 seconds.

The iX4 features a distinct coupe-SUV-like silhouette rather than the traditional boxy, upright SUV design of the iX3. With a rakish roofline and an aerodynamic design, the new iX4 has a drag coefficient of just 0.23.

Like the iX3, the iX4 is based on BMW’s Neue Klasse architecture with its sixth-generation (Gen6) eDrive system.

While EPA figures have yet to be finalized, BMW mentioned the new iX4 has an estimated driving range of up to 428 miles on a single charge using a 112.2 kWh battery. Under WLTP conditions, it offers an all-electric range of up to 514 miles (828 km).

It has been revealed that thanks to its 800V architecture, BMW’s newly introduced iX4 can add up to 184 miles of range (384 km on the WLTP cycle) in just 10 minutes with charging speeds of up to 400 kW. Charging the vehicle from 10% to 80% takes about 21 minutes.

Recent findings suggest that like BMW’s other Neue Klasse models, the new iX4 features its updated interior design. The setup includes a large 17.9″ infotainment screen and BMW’s new Panoramic Vision, a 42″ display spanning the base of the windshield.

It has been revealed that the iX4 is 188.3″ long, 74.6″ wide, and 63.3″ tall, with a 114.1″ wheelbase, which is about the same size as the iX3. However, it’s slightly lower than the iX3 thanks to the sloped roofline.

Like all Gen6 BMW models, the newly introduced iX4 supports bidirectional charging, enabling it to be used as a mobile power source for e-bikes, camping equipment, or other electrical devices.

In a recent development, the fresh BMW iX4 50 xDrive will go on sale in March 2027, starting at $66,300, or $4,800 more than the iX3 50 xDrive. That doesn’t include the $1,495 destination fee.

Sources indicate that arc Raiders just cannot be stopped. The extraction shooter from Embark Studios has once again attracted more players over the weekend than it has in its launch week, and over its first weekend on the market.

The positive reception the PvPvE game has garnered from players has clearly caused many of them to convince their friends to jump into this unique gem of a game.

Sources indicate that the day Arc Raiders launched, it peaked at 264,673 concurrent players on Steam. Although not massive, it was quite a bit more than the game’s most popular - free - beta test managed to attract.

In a recent development, that figure was broken yet again over the game’s first weekend, with Arc Raiders having reached 354,836 concurrent players on Steam. This is where many thought it would settle, as we start to see the gradual - and expected - decline of player numbers.

To everyone’s surprise, however, Arc Raiders shattered even that record yet again on Sunday, November 9. According to SteamDB, the game peaked at 462,488 concurrent players on Steam, which is a sizeable increase on its launch day numbers. Indeed, should this trend continue, Arc Raiders is going to be well on its way to doubling its initial launch record.

While a few games have broken their launch Steam player records in the past, it’s incredibly rare to see it happen - especially twice in such a short period after launch. Embark clearly has a winner on its hands here.

In a recent development, arc Raiders’ next massive moment is the game’s first post-launch map, which is set to arrive at some point this month, alongside new Quests and other gameplay items. Seeing as how the Steam concurrent record has been broken twice, there’s every chance the arrival of the new map will bring another boost to player numbers.

If you’re among the millions of players who have been exploring the Rust Belt, you’re probably wondering where to find prickly pears, where to find lemons and apricots, and where to find olives - and those links will answer all of those questions. And, if you just jumped in over the weekend, you’re definitely going to find these Arc Raiders tips very helpful.

Theft is in the name, so what better way to strategy a good heist than to have a good understanding of how the map system works in Grand Theft Auto 6? Well, thankfully, we have the solution for you. If you are wondering if you’re able to enter a specific property, there is an easy and handy way to identify it on the map. This guide will go over just how to do so.

There’s a surprisingly well-designed feature in the map that no one really ever tells you about. Rockstar has created both a 2D and 3D virtual map for you to set waypoints, filter certain facilities and see where you haven’t been yet.

Recent findings suggest that one aspect of it is color. The coloring scheme is very handy not only in the open world (especially during your focus), but also in the map. By opening up a map, you will find essentially two different colors for houses and structures.

Sources indicate that if a structure is light blue, that means you won’t be able to get inside. If that structure is dark blue, that means you’ll be able to enter it. This can be done either through a doorway (where you can use a Snap Gun to avoid alarms or breaking in through brute force), or through a garage.

In a recent development, with that mentioned, not every dark blue structure can be accessed only because there are some that are tied specifically to the story and side missions. You will be able to move around in these houses during these quests but not in the open world.

Industry observers note that one of the best parts of Grand Theft Auto 6 is just exploring. Rockstar has created a breathtaking world to adventure, be it through the various missions or just going out on your own and creating havoc for yourself.

There are two aspects to why you’d go through these houses. The first is obviously to rob them or find collectibles. This is very much encouraged for more bigger locations such as banks, stores and so forth.

For standard houses, it’s all about environmental storytelling. Whether it’s coming across a house with what looks like a person who was recently tortured, a house with a disturbing number of female mannequins in it or a football player with a ton of trophies and footballs on display, Rockstar has created a fantastic world to just poke your nose in.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s no secret that electric cars are more affordable to maintain than their gasoline-powered counterparts. While they may have a higher purchase price than a comparable gas-powered vehicle, EVs can save owners money over time by eliminating the need for regular engine oil changes, emissions tests, and other traditional maintenance tasks. Affordable electric vehicles are also becoming increasingly common, with even more options expected to arrive in the coming years.

It has been revealed that however, that doesn't mean electric cars are completely maintenance-free. Like any other vehicle, EVs require regular care and attention to remain reliable and perform at their best for many years.

Although they don't have conventional combustion engines or traditional automatic transmissions, electric cars still feature components that require periodic maintenance. These include reduction gearboxes, brake fluid, brake pads, coolant systems, and tires among other things. Keeping these components in good condition is essential to ensuring an EV's long-term reliability.

ERANGE EV tires are purpose-built for electric vehicles, combining efficiency, comfort and performance with advanced EcoPoint3 technology.

For the second installment of our EV maintenance series, I'll be taking a closer look at the Hyundai Ioniq 5, one of the most recognizable electric crossovers on the market. Made in the United States and South Korea, the Ioniq 5 has long been one of the biggest rivals to the ubiquitous Tesla Model Y.

I'll break down Hyundai's recommended maintenance schedule, explaining which items are required to keep the vehicle running smoothly over the long term.

Compared to Tesla, which is known for its rather skimpy maintenance strategy, Hyundai includes a generous list of maintenance items in the owner’s manual. The automaker also includes additional service actions that should be performed if the car is used in harsher-than-normal conditions, so owners know what to expect in the long run.

It has been revealed that there’s a normal maintenance schedule and a separate section for severe usage and low mileage conditions. Hyundai also has a list of maintenance items that can be performed by the owner. I’ll go through all of them, so drivers can easily mark down what needs to be done during the car’s lifetime.

Hyundai says that normal driving conditions include distances longer than 10 miles, clean roads without salt or dust, ambient temperatures under 90ºF (32ºC), no towing, no roof rack, and normal speeds. Under these conditions, the required maintenance for a Hyundai Ioniq 5 is as follows, according to the owner’s manual:.

According to recent reports, according to Hyundai, extra precaution needs to be taken if the car is driven under certain conditions. These include repeated driving short distances of less than five miles in normal temperatures or less than 10 miles in freezing temperatures, and driving on rough, dusty, muddy, unpaved, graveled, or salt-spread roads.

But that’s not all. Driving in areas using salt or other corrosive materials, or in very cold weather, driving in heavy dust conditions, driving in heavy traffic areas with the ambient temperature higher than 90ºF (32 ºC) while consuming more than 50% of electric energy, and driving on uphill, downhill, or mountain roads repeatedly can also result in extra maintenance items.

Towing a trailer, using a roof rack, driving as a patrol car or taxi, frequently driving at high speeds, and frequently driving in stop-and-go conditions are also part of the conditions that lead to more intense servicing requirements.

In addition to the normal maintenance schedule above, Hyundai recommends the following actions for severe usage and low-mileage conditions:.

All of these items should be performed by a Hyundai technician, but the Ioniq 5 also has a consistent list of maintenance actions that should be performed by the owner.

The Hyundai Ioniq 5 is one of the best-selling electric crossovers in the United States, and for good reason. Its unique styling has plenty of fans, and it’s a genuinely nice car to drive. As for its maintenance requirements, the official recommendations have a lot more items compared to the Tesla Model Y, but at the end of the day, most of them are just inspection jobs. As a result, maintenance costs should be quite low compared to a comparable gas vehicle. Just rotate and replace tires, keep an eye on your brakes, and swap out the coolant after 10 years or 120,000 miles.

Tesla FSD v15 is AI4’s last shot as Musk reveals how little compute is left

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1600 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, tesla’s FSD v15 is its last real shot at delivering unsupervised self-driving on the AI4 computer in millions of customer cars.
  • He also confirmed that cars won’t get the next-gen AI5 chip, and that the mid-cycle AI4.5 upgrade just had its RAM cut from 32GB to 24GB.
  • According to recent reports, the most visible part of FSD v15 is Tesla Reality View, a live, video-game-like rendering of the car’s surroundings with chevrons floating in the sky for upcoming turns.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, tesla’s FSD v15 is its last real shot at delivering unsupervised self-driving on the AI4 computer in millions of customer cars. Elon Musk spent the weekend explaining on X how the newly introduced software uses the hardware, and there isn’t much room left.

He also confirmed that cars won’t get the next-gen AI5 chip, and that the mid-cycle AI4.5 upgrade just had its RAM cut from 32GB to 24GB.

According to recent reports, the most visible part of FSD v15 is Tesla Reality View, a live, video-game-like rendering of the car’s surroundings with chevrons floating in the sky for upcoming turns. Musk called it “real-time AI video generation (no gaming engine!) using just half of one AI4 TRIP accelerator.”.

According to recent reports, the fan accounts ran with that as a flex. But Musk’s follow-up posts tell a different story.

Industry observers note that he explained that after Tesla moved a decoder into SRAM, “we only have half a TRIP out of three on SoC B, for this reality visualizer, so spent the compute as best we could.” In other words, half a TRIP is what was left over. He added that TRIP, Tesla’s neural accelerator, “basically only handles 8-bit int and has to run softmax in emulation mode in 28 steps.”.

In another post, Musk described Reality View as a roughly 1-billion-parameter diffusion model running off the same vision encoder features “that are plugged into the 3B encoder model that produces the driving actions.” He admitted the visualization’s latency is “a bit high due to compute constraints.”.

That 3B figure is worth noting. Tesla talked up a 10x jump in FSD model size for over a year, first for v14 and then for v15. Musk didn’t say whether 3B covers the entire driving stack, but it’s nowhere near 10x.

And Tesla’s own engineers aren’t describing a chip with lots of headroom. Dilreet Raju, who works on Tesla’s AI silicon, wrote that the hardest work of his life was co-designing the v15 vision encoder “to squeeze out the last few percents of MFU from AI4.” MFU is model FLOPs utilization, a measure of how much of the chip’s theoretical compute the model actually uses. Musk replied with a target emoji.

It has been revealed that when Tesla unveiled its FSD computer in 2019, the selling point was redundancy: two independent chips on one board, each with its own power and memory, so one could take over if the other failed. As we noted when Tesla started shipping the AI4.5 computer in Model Y in January, Tesla’s FSD computers have historically used two identical chips for exactly that reason.

It has been revealed that that’s what an unsupervised, Level 4 system needs. With nobody in the driver’s seat, a hardware fault can’t simply hand control back to a human. The car needs enough healthy compute left to keep seeing the road and pull over safely.

According to recent reports, but Musk’s own description highlights SoC B running the decoder and the Reality View model, not sitting idle as a mirror of SoC A. Tesla hackers, including greentheonly, have reported for years that Tesla started splitting its FSD workload across both chips back in the HW3 days.

Tesla has never explained how much of AI4 it reserves for failover, or whether a single SoC can run enough of the stack to bring a car to a safe stop on its own. The more of the board v15 needs, the harder that question gets.

Waymo has answered it publicly. The organization says both of its onboard computing systems run full workloads in parallel and that a secondary computer can bring the vehicle to a safe stop if the primary fails, backed by redundant braking, steering and power. Its fresh custom chip is rated at more than 1,000 TOPS. By our own comparison of AI4 and Nvidia’s Drive Thor, AI4 is estimated at roughly 100 to 150 TOPS across both chips.

Industry observers note that tesla started rolling out FSD v15 on Saturday, claiming “25x better handling of safety critical cases” without any baseline. So far, the people posting videos are mostly the usual crowd of Tesla-focused accounts that get early builds. Just hours before the rollout started, Musk wrote that v15 “goes to wide release next month.”.

The early clips are almost all about Reality View, the fresh parking spot selection, and the floating arrows. Those are UI features. They say very little about how many miles v15 can drive between critical interventions, which is the only number that matters for unsupervised driving.

Recent findings suggest that that brings us to AI4.5. On Tesla’s Q1 2026 earnings call, Musk declared an “AI4 Plus” with RAM doubled from 16GB to 32GB per chip, which raised the question of whether HW4 would follow HW3.

In a recent development, this weekend, Musk said “AI4.5 is a relatively small performance improvement that is mostly due to needing to upgrade RAM to LPDDR5X.” Hours later, he added: “RAM is super expensive, so we reduced AI4.5 from 32GB to 24GB. That will be fine. It’s hard to use 32GB anyway, given memory bandwidth constraints.”.

He also said that AI4 “costs twice as much now due to memory and storage price hikes.”.

According to recent reports, so the mid-cycle refresh exists mainly because Tesla needs a newer memory type it can actually buy, not to unlock bigger models. If memory bandwidth is the bottleneck, as Musk keeps repeating, adding capacity doesn’t change much.

According to recent reports, asked by an owner on Sunday whether to wait for AI5 before upgrading from HW3, Musk answered: “It’s going to Optimus. Cars will remain at AI4. That’s enough to solve superhuman driving.”.

Sources indicate that an interesting comment, as it destroys one thing that HW3 owners were holding to: Tesla was delaying HW3 upgrades until it had AI5. Now, it’s clearly not the case and Tesla has no excuse not to upgrade HW3 cars.

He described AI5 as “a gigantic improvement. Roughly 12X more compute,” and later as “roughly an order of magnitude hardware performance improvement, all things considered. Memory bandwidth is a constraint.” Last year, he said that by some metrics AI5 would be 40 times better than AI4.

Recent findings suggest that AI5 is also moving around. In October, Musk mentioned Tesla cut AI5’s RAM in half to 72GB to get enough volume for Optimus, then nudged it back up to 96GB a day later. AI6 was cut by a third, to 144GB of LPDDR6. When asked about AI6 this weekend, Musk replied with a chef’s kiss meme.

As we reported in July, Samsung’s Texas fab won’t reach AI5 volume production until the second half of 2027, nearly two years behind Musk’s original timeline. And that volume is now headed to robots and data centers, not cars.

This is the situation for AI4 owners: v15 has to be the one. And we heard Elon Musk calling every FSD upgrade “the one” for the last decade.

According to recent reports, tesla’s own engineers are talking about squeezing the last few percent of utilization out of AI4. Musk describes a half-accelerator scrap of compute left for the visualizer. The AI4.5 refresh is a RAM swap that just got downsized, and AI5 isn’t coming to cars. If v15 can’t get to unsupervised driving on AI4, there’s no hardware escape hatch for the fleet.

BTW, I've reached out to Tesla to ask how they handle compute redundancy, but I don't expect a response.

We’ve seen this movie before. Tesla said HW3 was enough for unsupervised self-driving until it wasn’t, and those owners are still waiting on an answer about upgrades. AI4 owners paid for the same promise.

And even if v15 drives well, I want to know how Tesla handles a chip failure with nobody behind the wheel. That’s not optional for Level 4. If the stack needs both SoCs to drive, what brings the car to a safe stop when one of them crashes?

According to recent reports, as for v15 itself, I’m not drawing conclusions from influencer clips. Reality View looks great, but it’s also visibly laggy, and Musk admits it’s compute-limited. A great visual upgrade is nice. Driving performance is what matters. I’ll wait until I get it in my own car to see how significant the improvement actually is.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Riot will take the Mid-Season Invitational to Spain in 2027, bringing a top-tier League of Legends event back to Europe for the first time since the Worlds 2024 final in London. Its one-off, expanded First Stand in China will also change Split 1 for the LEC, with the full details due in January.

In a recent development, europe will host a top-tier League of Legends event again in 2027. Riot set out its international calendar on 13 November, the eve of the Worlds 2026 final. The Mid-Season Invitational goes to Valencia. London’s staging of the Worlds 2024 final was the last time the continent held an international League of Legends tournament.

For British fans, that puts a top-tier event within Europe next year. Riot has not yet given dates or ticket details for the Feria de Valencia event.

Spain’s last international League of Legends event came in 2019. That year, Madrid’s Palacio Vistalegre staged the Worlds quarter-finals and semi-finals. Valencia has never hosted one before.

According to recent reports, china will stage First Stand: All In at the start of the 2027 season. Riot calls this single edition its largest tournament ever.

It has been revealed that first Stand 2027 had originally been given to Southeast Asia. The bigger format took it to China instead. Southeast Asia will now host the event in 2028.

The change reaches every regional league, including the LEC. The larger event will change Split 1, just as Fnatic, G2 and the other LEC teams rebuild their rosters. In 2026, First Stand ran from 16 to 22 March, between the two regional splits. A bigger event at the start of the year leaves less certainty about how that window will look in 2027.

Sources indicate that riot has not yet said how many teams will take part or how they will qualify. Until then, LEC teams are building squads without knowing how many European places are on offer.

Worlds 2027 will be shared between two countries. The Swiss Stage goes to Nagoya, Japan. The quarter-finals and semi-finals move to the Suwon Convention Center in South Korea. The title decider goes to Seoul Arena, which is still under construction.

The arena was 81% built on 23 October. Work is due to finish in May 2027, with the venue opening in June 2027.

The city is backing the event with public money. Seoul has set aside 1.369 billion won (about US$1.02 million) in its proposed 2027 budget to host the Worlds final and Fan Fest, Sheep Esports reported.

In a recent development, the 2026 calendar offers a reference point for the circuit’s rhythm. MSI ran from 28 June to 12 July, and Worlds from 15 October to 14 November. Riot has not confirmed whether the 2027 events will follow similar windows.

For LEC teams, clarity on the season opener in China is due in January.

This latest release is also the first to tackle some of the problems players have been running into playing Redsec battle royale, the free-to-play component that also came out recently.

Patch 1.1.1.5 is fairly limited in scope. The biggest fix in this one comes to the Lock-Guided Missiles going through flares, and generally being annoying enough to stop players from using air vehicles altogether.

According to recent reports, the Lock-Guided Missiles were mainly used by AA vehicles, but they could also be equipped by IFVs, which made it even more of a nightmare to pilots. It got so bad that Battlefield Studios disabled it entirely while the team worked on a proper fix.

Another exploit the patch fixes is the one that allowed players to stand on the Recon Drone and reach areas they’re not supposed to. This was done by… repeatedly hitting it with a Sledgehammer. The long-running concern of vehicles not spawning for certain teams in Conquest and Breakthrough appears to have finally been fixed, too.

It has been revealed that in terms of battle royale, the patch has a few fixes that should help make the experience more consistent, as well as improve the flow of matches. One of the more interesting addresses an concern that could eliminate the entire squad instead of reviving dead teammates when using a Mobile Spawn.

Patch 1.1.1.5 also has yet more adjustments to weapon dispersion (bloom). Some of the casses it addresses include transitioning from sprint to firing in ADS, and others where it apparently scaled with player movement speed.

GTA 6: How to Get into the Airport

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (424 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Whether it’s driving around the vast city skyline of Vice City, boating in the Pacific Ocean or taking to the skies, there’s no shortage of ways to see Grand Theft Auto 6 in all of its beauty.
  • Recent findings suggest that there are a couple of ways to get into the airport, not one being through the arrivals or departure terminals.
  • Probably the easiest way to get in is flying in from a helicopter or from a plane you obtained from the early portions of the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Whether it’s driving around the vast city skyline of Vice City, boating in the Pacific Ocean or taking to the skies, there’s no shortage of ways to see Grand Theft Auto 6 in all of its beauty. While you won’t be taking planes to Liberty City or Los Santos, you can break into the airport and steal a plane.

Recent findings suggest that there are a couple of ways to get into the airport, not one being through the arrivals or departure terminals. To start things off, you will need to know where it’s located. The VCIA (Vice City International Airport) is located near the middle of the map, just west of the Salton district.

Probably the easiest way to get in is flying in from a helicopter or from a plane you obtained from the early portions of the game. You will be picked up pretty swiftly as the threshold for the radar is low, but it’s definitely the simplest method in finding your way in. Driving in is also an option as there are various checkpoints you can slam right through.

Outside these options, there are some really easy entrances to the airport if you don’t have a plane or helicopter at your disposal. While driving is probably the way to go, there are fences on the east and west portions of the map that can get in from.

Most of it is barbed, but you will find some that is a simple fence to hop over (as shown in the photo). Simply jump over and sneak around. People will notice you if you come in view of them, so steal a vehicle as quick as possible, but even the, they have trackers.

Unfortunately, when you steal a commercial vehicle such as a Dreamliner in Grand Theft Auto 6, things are not going to go well for you. People will immediately notice when an aircraft isn’t supposed to leave and takes off.

If you completed most of chapter 4 of the story, you’ll know that the airport has numerous safety measures, including snipers perched on every corner. On top of that, air traffic control will immediately catch wind of what you’re doing.

According to recent reports, sadly, when you get off the ground, you will be met with multiple stars, and they will immediately call-in fighter jets. If you don’t put the plane down, they will do so forcefully. You will have a limited amount of time to finish your joyride before it’s removed from the air permanently.

Sources indicate that it’s pretty clear at this stage that Arc Raiders is one of the biggest releases of 2025. More interesting than the numbers themselves, however, is that this is an extraction shooter - a subgenre which has typically been thought of as niche.

If you’ve been paying the PvPvE game any attention, you could easily see how (and why) it keeps breaking its own records.

Industry observers note that today, publisher Nexon announced in a press release (via Gematsu) that Arc Raiders has now sold over 4 million copies. The game came out on October 30, which means it managed to sell that many copies in a little over 10 days.

Sources indicate that the news comes on the same day that developer Embark Studios announced that the game had more than 700,000 concurrent players across all platforms over the weekend. Over the same weekend on Steam alone, Arc Raiders broke its own Steam concurrent record with a latest peak of 462,488 players - which is a significant chunk of that 700,000+ player base.

Recent findings suggest that this marks the second time the extraction shooter has broken its own concurrent player records, which is something very few games have managed in the past. Arc Raiders remains a top-seller, too. On Steam, it’s right now the second-best seller globally (by revenue), sitting just below Counter-Strike 2.

It has been revealed that “The many different ways you play and participate in ARC Raiders have completely blown us away, going far beyond what we ever imagined. You surprise us, you outsmart us, and you keep us on our toes. We wouldn’t have it any other way,” the developer wrote on Twitter.

Embark recently published a roadmap to highlight all the upcoming content coming to the game over the remainder of this year. The first new map is set to arrive this month alongside new Arc units, new gameplay items, new events and more.

Sources indicate that just over the weekend, the game received several new Map Conditions that completely alter the way they play. The developer has already rolled out a couple of updates since launch, in order to tackle exploits and fix a few launchday bugs.

If you’re right now hooked on this gem of a game, we guarantee that our Arc Raiders gameplay tips will have at least one you didn’t know about. We also have more guides on how to find some of the more elusive items in the game, such as olives, lemons and apricots, and prickly pears.

Industry observers note that as many of Arc Raiders’ regular players predicted, the game’s first post-launch map won’t just be available for everyone, it will instead be closely tied to a community event. Breaking Latest Ground is the name of that event, and it’s one where everyone will need to contribute in order to rebuild some old tunnels and unlock the way to Stella Montis.

In a recent development, the event kicks off today alongside the release of the game’s latest patch. The ask is relatively simple: players must commit Basic Materials to the project so that the tunnels can be rebuilt. This option will be available to anyone who’s played at least five rounds.

If you’ve spent any time in Arc Raiders, you’ll know that Basic Materials are things like Metal parts, Fabric, Chemicals, Rubber Parts, and Plastic Parts - most of which are easy to find in the game’s various maps.

Even beyond the ultimate goal of unlocking the fresh map, donations will also reward you with Merits, which is a new event currency, though there’s a cap on how many you can earn.

Once enough materials have been collected, the next phase of the event, Staking Our Claim, will begin, which will bring a new progression track to the game, and make Stella Montis available for players to visit.

Sources indicate that developer Embark describes the new environment as unlike any that we have seen in the game so far. It’s a facility carved into the northern mountains, which means it’s going to have a near-pristine look; quite the contrast with the rest of the game’s environments.

Stella Montis also has its own Arc enemies, loot, schematics, and other gameplay items. You can look forward to coming across the Shredder, a close-quarter Arc unit exclusive to the new map for now.

Recent findings suggest that then there’s The Matriarch, a somehow even larger version of the Queen. Thankfully, it will only be available under a specific map condition, so you’re in no danger of running into her randomly. The revision will also introduce a new legendary weapon, two new grenades, and three new mines.

It has been revealed that staking Our Claim will only run until December, which is when the next stage of the game’s roadmap will kick off. Then, the Cold Snap upgrade will introduce the Flickering Flames event, the first snowfall Map Condition, and the Expedition Project voluntary wipe.

In case you’re still missing them, here’s how to find lemons and apricots, prickly pear, and olives.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toyota is overhauling its best-selling vehicle of all time, which will include the first fully electric Corolla.

The Toyota Corolla is one of the most recognized and best-selling automotive nameplates of all time.

Since its debut in 1966, over 57 million drivers have chosen the Corolla thanks to its reliability, low cost of ownership, efficiency, and affordable price tag.

Toyota sells the Corolla in more than 150 countries and has expanded the lineup over the past 50 years from sedans and hatchbacks to coupes, wagons, a sporty GR Corolla, and the Corolla Cross compact SUV.

For its 13th generation, Toyota is planning a major overhaul that’s expected to be its biggest transformation yet.

The next-gen Toyota Corolla will be based on a new “multipathway” platform that will support gas, hybrid, plug-in hybrid, and, for the first time, fully electric powertrains.

“Whether it’s a battery EV, plug-in hybrid, hybrid, or internal combustion engine vehicle ― whatever the power source ― let’s make good-looking cars that everyone will want to drive!” Toyota’s former president and current CEO Koji Sato said after unveiling the Corolla Concept at the Japan Mobility Show last October.

Toyota has kept most details a secret, including battery and powertrain specs. However, the newly introduced version is expected to adopt a similar design to the concept.

“When we created the concept, we wanted to give the Corolla name a latest twist,” Norihiko Kobayashi, who has led the Corolla program since 2011, told Motor.es during a recent interview.

The Corolla has undergone several minor updates over the past 60 years, but the next-gen model will look nothing like its predecessors.

“It wasn’t simply about following in the footsteps of the past,” Kobayashi explained, “we wanted to delve into the future while still maintaining the Corolla identity.”.

Developing the next-gen Corolla “wasn’t just about making a fresh car, but about redefining the future without looking back,” he added.

Like the current version, the upcoming Toyota Corolla will come in several different body types, including a sedan, hatchback, crossover, and a GR variant.

The Corolla was the entry level vehicle for a lot of people before they could afford the Camry or the Lexus.

Details have yet to be confirmed, but the Toyota Corolla EV is expected to be available in single- and dual-motor configurations and offer a pure electric driving range of at least 250 miles.

Industry observers note that the hybrid will reportedly use a newly introduced 1.5-liter four-cylinder engine and an electric motor. Toyota’s engineers told Car and Driver the hybrid system would deliver around 134 horsepower. It’s also estimated to be 10% to 20% more efficient than the current Corolla.

Sources indicate that toyota’s next-gen Corolla is expected to debut sometime in 2027 as a 2028 model year. According to Car and Driver, the gas version will likely start at around $25,000, the hybrid around $27,000, and the EV and PHEVs will likely be priced in the $30,000 range.

Earlier this month, the next-gen Toyota Corolla Cross was spotted testing for the first time (see the images here).

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gameinformer ↗ Open Full Page

The Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Easter Eggs That Did And Did Not Make It Into The 2026 Remake

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (923 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo 64 is a game full of Easter Eggs, secrets, and hidden mechanics (did you know if a butterfly lands on your Deku Stick, it summons a fairy?).
  • It has been revealed that in the courtyard where Link first meets Zelda, there is arguably the most fourth-wall-breaking Easter Egg in the whole game.
  • For the 2026 remake, there are no references to other Nintendo characters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo 64 is a game full of Easter Eggs, secrets, and hidden mechanics (did you know if a butterfly lands on your Deku Stick, it summons a fairy?). Now in its second remake, not every secret has made its way forward through the previous iterations, but many have. Below you will learn about a few of the secrets that made the cut, and others that didn’t.

It has been revealed that in the courtyard where Link first meets Zelda, there is arguably the most fourth-wall-breaking Easter Egg in the whole game. If you don’t rush to Zelda and instead pause and enter first-person to look around, you will see portraits of other Nintendo characters through the windows, like Mario and Yoshi. In the 3DS remake, the portraits are replaced by an image of a Mario stage.

For the 2026 remake, there are no references to other Nintendo characters. Instead, the tapestry you build over the course of the game is on display. Removing the reference to Nintendo characters outside of the Zelda universe is understandable, but it is a little odd that art representing the full adventure of the game – an adventure that has not yet concluded – is on the wall.

According to recent reports, as stated above, the Nintendo character portraits are gone, but there is still a guard you can annoy. If you fire a Deku Seed into the left window, a guard will pop out, yell at you, and then throw a bomb at you. You can’t pick up the bomb. In fact, at this point in the game, you haven’t even seen a bomb.

Recent findings suggest that the Hyrule Castle portrait references to Yoshi and Mario are gone (though Mario and Luigi are still kind of in the game in a way), but Bowser gets a pass for some reason. Both Malon and her dad, Talon, are still wearing Bowser pins on their clothes. And unlike the N64 game where the detail was a little vague, there is no mistaking it here.

Gossip Stones are all over Ocarina of Time and it takes a while to understand what they do. If you hit them with a sword, they tell you the time, and if you play Zelda’s Lullaby near them, they refill your magic. If you do the Happy Mask Salesman’s side quest, interacting with them while wearing the Mask of Truth offers little hints and details about the world. But then there are interactions that are just odd for no reason. Blowing up a bomb near a Gossip Stone still makes it take off like a rocket ship, and using the Megaton Hammer still flattens them for a moment like a Looney Tunes.

And speaking of playing Zelda’s Lullaby for inanimate objects, if you slash a sign to pieces with your sword and regret your words and deeds, you can play the iconic tune to make the signs reform and become readable again.

Industry observers note that this detail was exclusive to the 3DS remake of Ocarina of Time, and surprising no one, it has been removed. Ocarina of Time launched in June 2011 and Nintendo released Skyward Sword about five months later in November. For… marketing purposes, I guess, Skyward Sword art could be found in Lonlon Ranch, the Bombchu Shop in Hyrule Castle Town, and the Gerudo Fortress. It was a fun Easter Egg to discover back in 2011, especially since Skyward Sword was still months away, but these days it’s a bit of an odd inclusion.

Sources indicate that though never explicit, the composer ghosts guarding the Sun’s Song (and Link’s first ReDead encounter) have always been assumed to be inspired by Mario and Luigi. They are brothers; Flat is short, squat, and red; Sharp is lanky and green. They still appear in Ocarina of Time this way, which isn't surprising, since they are vital characters you must meet to get a very useful song. Fans have also speculated that Talon and Ingo are Mario and Luigi-inspired for similar reasons, but it’s worth noting that they are not brothers.

In the Spirit Temple there is a large statue of a woman and for reasons that have never been explained, Link could attach his hookshot to her breasts. It served no purpose. It didn’t help solve a puzzle. If anything, it was confusing. But we all tried it and there is no shame in admitting it! That was removed for the 3DS remake, and it remains removed in 2026.

Industry observers note that this is a very subtle reference to Wind Waker/Breath of the Wild/Tears of the Kingdom and is potentially the only addition to the remake that looks toward the future of the Zelda franchise. Obviously, plenty of characters in Ocarina later appear in Majora’s Mask (another remake of that is hopefully being considered), but it would be inaccurate to call those intentional Easter Eggs.

However, in Kokiri Forest and in the neighboring Lost Woods, the magical debris floating in the air often resembles a Korok as it would later appear in the series. It makes sense, too, because the Koroks are meant to be what the Kokiri transformed into following The Great Flood.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that slate made a substantial splash with its affordable, heavily customizable electric truck.
  • The La Bagnole is one of the most interesting looking cars I've ever seen, It looks like a French Willy's Jeep but with the fully open wheels of F1 car.
  • In a recent development, both versions come with an optional removable roof, which is pretty awesome.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that slate made a substantial splash with its affordable, heavily customizable electric truck. Someone even copied the formula over to a lineup of gas-powered trucks, and we'll see another cheap electric truck from Ford next year. But now the French have their own cheap electric truck concept. It's called the Kilow La Bagnole (which literally translates to "the car"), and it's adorable. I need one.

The La Bagnole is one of the most interesting looking cars I've ever seen, It looks like a French Willy's Jeep but with the fully open wheels of F1 car. It only seats two and two different kinds of body styles, Hard Top (basically a pickup truck) and Closed Hard Top (becomes a van). Both can be had with roof bars so you can put all sorts of gear up there. If you get the Hard Top, the side bed rails are made from either resin-bonded wood fiber or Okoume wood. The former makes it look like it's from IKEA, while the latter looks more premium. However, the Okoume wood requires periodic to keep it weather proof.

In a recent development, both versions come with an optional removable roof, which is pretty awesome. So you can have either a targa-top pickup or van. The standard La Bagnole lacks doors, and only has major metal side bars, but you can option transparent doors, which are neat.

If you want colors, boy can you get 'em. Kilow offers 12 different regular color options, six gradient colors, and six sparkly "Memories" colors. The best part is that they're all free options. The chassis of the La Bagnole is steel, but all of its body panels are easy removable. So if one breaks or dents, you can just replace it.

According to recent reports, there are a few different battery options. Two of the options are made to allow unlicensed drivers to use them. Both the 6 kWh and 12 kWh "Long Range" batteries require no license, as they're classified as quadricycles and capped at 45 km/h (28 mph). Trucks with the 6 kWh battery have only 70 km (43 miles) of range. Cars with the 12 kWh battery can go 164 km (102 miles). The third option mates the 12 kWh battery with an increased speed limiter of 80 km/h (50 mph), but that requires a driver's license.

Industry observers note that I love this little thing, and I wish it was coming to the United States. As of right now, it will only be offered in Europe, starting in France. The La Bagnole is such a charming, fun looking little utility vehicle that seems designed equally for function and form. With prices ranging from €10,800 ($11,758) - €13,690 ($14,904), it's an affordable work vehicle for anyone who needs one and stays local, but with tons of character.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that getting a helicopter is one of the better ways to travel in Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • Industry observers note that you can definitely jump out and parachute to where you’re going, but then you’ve lost your means of transportation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

How you travel in Grand Theft Auto 6 is very vital. Whether it’s by plane, train or automobile, there’s a slew of different ways to get around the vast world Rockstar has created. One of them is a helicopter. This is an iconic vehicle from the franchise that gets you to places faster than most, but securing one isn’t exactly the easiest thing to do. Thankfully, with this guide, you’ll be able to find them with ease.

Recent findings suggest that getting a helicopter is one of the better ways to travel in Grand Theft Auto 6. While planes are faster and bring you further distances, there isn’t always a good way to park them. You can definitely try landing on some rugged piece of land or on the freeway, but the chances it will work or stay there when you come back is unlikely – not to mention the chances of getting back into the sky are unlikely.

Industry observers note that you can definitely jump out and parachute to where you’re going, but then you’ve lost your means of transportation. That’s where helicopters come into play. They are a good middle ground where they can cover a good amount of ground fast and be more versatile when it comes to escape vehicles.

Heck, during robberies, parking this out back is always handy if cops aren’t at the ready when you exit the building. While you’ll be unable to register helicopters as personal vehicles, having a good idea where they are located is always good.

According to recent reports, early on, there are very few actual helicopters to speak of. You will be able to find a couple of helicopters that can land on water, but even they are rarer than water planes. Where you will need to look is in Vice City itself.

The easiest tell is looking at the map and looking for a helipad. The thing, though, is that not all helipads have helicopters on them. Some are meant for you to land on them instead of housing something for you to take.

You will want to look in three different districts of Vice City: Tequesta, Downtown and Washington Beach, specifically in that order to look for them.

According to recent reports, tequesta has arguably the most to choose from, but we’re assuming you’re coming from the south. From here, there will be a hotel all the way to the southeast of the area up against the water. Enter from the front and take the elevator all the way up.

If you’re coming from the south, the first place you should hit is the Rico Huxley Hotels. This is located on the river just east of the Zenith gym. Take the elevator up into the lobby and then break into the roof access area.

If you’ve made it to the fourth chapter, you’ll be pretty familiar with the area, but the Crimson Palms Condominiums is the place you need to go. This is up against the water to the north, two buildings south of the Aichi Condominiums Outdoor Gym. Like the others, take the elevator up and get onto the roof.

#98465. BYD Ti7 banned from the EU for copying the Land Rover Defender’s design

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1090 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

BYD Ti7 banned from the EU for copying the Land Rover Defender’s design

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1090 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Dutch court has barred BYD from selling or building its Ti7 SUV anywhere in the European Union after ruling that it infringes Jaguar Land Rover’s registered design for the Land Rover Defender.
  • It’s a sharp turnaround from 10 days ago, when the same court in The Hague handed BYD an early win in the Defender copycat fight.
  • The preliminary relief judge at the District Court of The Hague issued the ruling on Friday, November 20, in summary proceedings JLR brought against 11 BYD companies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Dutch court has barred BYD from selling or building its Ti7 SUV anywhere in the European Union after ruling that it infringes Jaguar Land Rover’s registered design for the Land Rover Defender. Breaking the injunction costs BYD €100,000 per day, up to €10 million.

It’s a sharp turnaround from 10 days ago, when the same court in The Hague handed BYD an early win in the Defender copycat fight. BYD’s Hong Kong shares fell as much as 4% on Monday before closing 1.9% lower.

The preliminary relief judge at the District Court of The Hague issued the ruling on Friday, November 20, in summary proceedings JLR brought against 11 BYD companies.

In a recent development, JLR put six registered EU designs in front of the court. The judge only needed one of them: design 005248580-0004, registered in April 2018 and covering the current Defender 110, known internally as the L663.

According to the ruling, the elements that dominate that design are the rounded “shoulders,” the rounded corners, the signature panel on the C-pillar, the rounded wheel-arch cutouts, the continuous window line, and the overall silhouette. The court found every one of them on the Ti7.

Here’s how the two SUVs compare from the same angles, using official press images from BYD and JLR:.

Sources indicate that BYD argued that the headlights, grille, bumpers, hood and side profile are all different. Not enough, said the judge, who ruled that those differences, on their own or combined, don’t give an informed user a different overall impression. The court also found the Ti7 sits closer to the Defender than to older boxy SUVs like the Ford Flex, Jeep Wrangler and Mercedes G-Class.

BYD doesn’t sell the Ti7 in the EU. It told the court it has “no concrete plans” to launch it there and that the SUV can only be ordered in the UK.

Industry observers note that the judge didn’t buy that as a defense. By BYD’s own account, it developed the seven-seat layout for the UK and Europe, a promotional video called the Ti7 the first seven-seat SUV “in Europe,” and BYD wouldn’t commit to keeping it out of the EU. That was enough for the court to find a threat of infringement.

In a recent development, so BYD’s EU entities can no longer import, produce, offer, sell, store or supply the Ti7. The order kicks in one week after the ruling is formally served, and it even covers BYD’s Hungarian unit, since the judge considered it conceivable the Ti7 could come out of the new Szeged factory.

The UK is a different story. The court stated it has no jurisdiction over BYD UK and threw out JLR’s UK design claims, so British deliveries are still on for January 2027. That’s the one European market where BYD actually opened orders, pricing the Ti7 at £47,995, about £24,000 below the £71,840 plug-in Defender 110.

BYD remarked it “strongly disagrees” with the judgment and will appeal, adding that the Ti7 “is the result of BYD’s own independent design work and infringes none of JLR’s rights.” JLR told AFP it protects its intellectual property and takes legal action when necessary.

BYD has four weeks to appeal, but the injunction stays in force while it does. JLR, for its part, has six months to file a full case on the merits, or BYD can get the injunction lifted.

Industry observers note that this whole thing started in August, when JLR had bailiffs raid BYD’s Dutch offices in Schiedam and Hoofddorp. The court later ordered JLR to destroy everything it seized, saying it didn’t need BYD’s internal files to make its design case. And it didn’t. JLR won on the design registration alone.

It has been revealed that the Ti7 looks like a Defender. We said so when BYD first brought it to the UK, and so did pretty much everyone else. Chinese automakers have been building Defender lookalikes for years, but most of them stayed in China.

BYD brought one to the Defender’s home turf at a £24,000 discount, so a fight with JLR was always coming.

"...ruled that those differences, on their own or combined, don’t give an informed user a different overall impression.".

Recent findings suggest that really? I feel like anyone who pays even a little attention to car designs isn't going to mistake the two. The thing most people see as differentiating within the same category is the headlights, tail lights, grill - which are all significantly different.

The only real similarity is the proportions, there are a ton of similarly proportioned SUVs but that's a result of the form factor.

But honestly, all these boxy SUVs look the same to me.

According to recent reports, nobody owns “boxy.” JLR even failed to trademark the classic Defender’s shape in the UK, a fight it lost in its legal battle with the Ineos Grenadier. But it registered the new Defender’s design in 2018, and that specific combination of shoulders, C-pillar panel and wheel arches is exactly what the court protected. That’s how design rights are supposed to work.

Industry observers note that the actual business damage is small for now. The Ti7 sells roughly 30,000 units a month, almost all in China, and the UK launch goes ahead. The stock dip was about headlines more than lost Ti7 sales.

#98463. Ford Has A Dedicated Battery Abuse Team. It Obsesses Over How Cells Fail

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (955 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Insideevs ↗ Open Full Page

Ford Has A Dedicated Battery Abuse Team. It Obsesses Over How Cells Fail

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (955 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Electric vehicle batteries live a harder life than the ones in your phone or laptop.
  • That means for battery makers, engineering for durability is a priority right up there with energy density and charging speed.
  • “That team is 100% focused on battery abuse, design, and testing as a function,” Wesley Thibault, the global chief engineer of battery product development at Ford stated last week during a media roundtable at the automaker’s new battery plant in Marshall, Michigan.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Electric vehicle batteries live a harder life than the ones in your phone or laptop. They spend most of their time outdoors, deal with extreme heat and cold, and can take a beating from road debris and potholes.

That means for battery makers, engineering for durability is a priority right up there with energy density and charging speed. And to make sure its cells can handle the abuse of daily life as an EV, Ford has a team dedicated to understanding how batteries fail—and how to stop it.

“That team is 100% focused on battery abuse, design, and testing as a function,” Wesley Thibault, the global chief engineer of battery product development at Ford stated last week during a media roundtable at the automaker’s new battery plant in Marshall, Michigan.

Recent findings suggest that ford is fresh to the EV battery business. Last week, it started cranking out lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery packs at BlueOval Battery Park Michigan, using technology licensed from China’s CATL, the world’s largest battery maker. The batteries will power the all-notable Ford Fathom pickup, which the automaker says will enter production toward the end of next year and kick off a new generation of vastly better and more profitable EVs.

Despite the licensing deal, Ford officials noted they were involved in developing the batteries from the outset, with a focus on durability.

Sources indicate that the job is not as simple as it sounds. The battery abuse team isn’t tasked with destroying fully made cells and then finding ways to make them indestructible. Instead, Thibault remarked, it is involved in the design process from the start.

“They want to understand down to the physics level, how a cell fails and why, and when it does fail, how we can prevent it from creating harm to the occupants,” he mentioned.

Quality operator at Ford's BlueOval Battery Park Michigan.

For example, the team measures how cells vent, a crucial process that keeps batteries from catching fire or damaging themselves when they overheat. When temperatures inside a cell get too high, the electrolyte, the liquid chemical that shuttles electrons between the anode and cathode, gets hot and releases gases.

If those gases stay trapped, they can cause short circuits or thermal runaway, so they need to escape in a controlled way. Thibault remarked his team can measure all of this analytically—using computer models—before the cells are validated.

It has been revealed that production adds another layer of scrutiny. At various stages, the materials inside the cell, as well as the finished cell itself, go through thousands of quality checks, Ford engineers said. Those include CT scans, X-ray machines, lasers, camera inspections, and AI systems.

Recent findings suggest that for example, when the anode slurry is coated onto a copper foil, every millimeter is scanned by lasers for wrinkles and other anomalies. All employees have the ability to pause production if they spot any problems.In case of any issues, they quarantine the cells affected during a specific time period. Ford also claimed that impacted components can be traced all the way from production to the vehicle they end up in.

To be sure, not all of this is unique to Ford. Strict quality checks like these are common among major battery makers, who all aim to minimize scrap rates for costly batteries and maximize the amount of material that actually gets sold.

Ford engineer operating a winding machine, which brings together the anode and cathode, adding a separator in between.

Ford continuously tests the manufacturing process in other ways, too. Engineers said they intentionally feed damaged components and cells—which they call “red rabbits”—into the production machinery to confirm the quality systems catch them and are working as intended.

When cells are almost ready, they’re blasted with helium gas to check for leaks. Once a pack is assembled, it’s mounted on a hydraulic shaker that mimics thousands of miles and years of real-world road use. The shaker can twist, dive, squat, contort, yaw, and replicate the other movements of a car, putting the pack through everything it would see on the road.

Ford’s EV batteries have fared well, by and large. High-mileage Mach-Es with 100,000 or even 200,000 miles on the odometer show little range loss compared to their original capacity, according to data the company released this month.

On the other hand, Ford’s emphasis on battery quality isn’t exactly surprising. The company has grappled with high warranty costs in recent years. And both the Mustang Mach-E and the F-150 Lightning have had issues linked to their high-voltage batteries. Some early Mach-Es were recalled because their battery contactors would overheat during DC fast-charging. A small number of Lightnings were recalled in 2023 due to defective battery cells.

Ford will want to avoid any similar quality challenges as it rolls out the high-stakes Fathom, which it hopes will outsell its previous EVs and set the stage for an electric comeback. It will be years before we know how the Fathom's batteries hold up in the real world. For now, it looks like the company is pulling out all the stops to make sure things go off without a hitch.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that battlefield 6’s first season has entered its second phase. The game received a major update earlier today, version 1.1.2.0, which delivers a host of changes to the game, many of which have been expected.

The revision, of course, also adds fresh content to the game in the form of the map Eastwood, as well as new hardware and fresh features for the multiplayer sandbox.

In a recent development, we’ve known about the new content side of today’s patch for quite some time. The revision kicks off the California Resistance stage of Season 1, which is the second of three. The new Eastwood map takes place in California, and it’s a map cut from the larger Battlefield Redsec battle royale map of Fort Lyndon.

There’s a new limited-time mode called Sabotage - a tactical, 8v8 mode where two teams attempt to destroy as many bomb sites as possible. The other substantial new feature that arrives today is Battle Pickups.

In a recent development, these are powerful weapons which can be found in specific game modes (and in Portal), scattered around the map for players to pick up and use. They have limited ammo that cannot be replenished, and deliver incredible firepower.

In a recent development, redsec players have a new Gauntlet mission to look forward to that joins the existing modes. It’s called Rodeo and it involves a lot of vehicular action. Finally, everyone gets to unlock two new weapons: the the DB-12 shotgun, and the M327 Trait revolver sidearm. There’s also a new angled grip attachment.

Sources indicate that the fixes and tweaks side of the patch is arguably the more interesting. Controller aim assist has received a massive overhaul that essentially resets everything to open beta settings. The goal is to make infantry targeting more consistent.

Industry observers note that controller players actually get the bulk of the changes in this enhancement, which also improves input latency and stick response. Several issues that reset aim assist values, or make it behave erratically, have been addressed.

The conversation around weapon bloom/spread doesn’t look like it’s ever going to end, because Battlefield Studios is yet again tuning gunplay to fix unintended dispersion behaviour, and decrease its intensity across the board.

Industry observers note that certain Challenges have had their description rewritten so their requirements can be better understood. Beyond that, you can expect several deployables to behave much more consistently, including several bug fixes there, too.

Head to the official blog for the full rundown of patch 1.1.2.0.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time hit Switch 2 today, and, as Kyle Hilliard pointed out in our review, it is pretty excellent.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time hit Switch 2 today, and, as Kyle Hilliard pointed out in our review, it is pretty excellent. Along with its remarkable visual upgrade, the fresh Switch 2 remake of Ocarina of Time adds quality-of-life improvements and modernizes the control scheme. As part of that, Nintendo has added the ability to jump and sprint. While that works well to make the game feel new, I swiftly realized it sometimes clashes with another new improvement: a free camera controlled by the right stick. Holding down the sprint button to get through areas as fast as possible can make it tricky to keep the camera where you want it, but thankfully, if you have the Switch 2 Pro Controller, there's an easy fix.

After hours of running around, I was awestruck by the level of detail and updates, but I found myself constantly fighting with the camera, or at the very least, needing to take a strange claw-style grip to be able to direct the camera with the right stick, while holding down the A button to sprint. If you're a casual Switch 2 player, you might not have even noticed the back buttons on the Pro Controller, or you just have no idea what they do. Those buttons can be remapped on a per-game basis and it's a simple process. Everyone has their own preferences, but, for example, for high-mobility shooters, I like remapping one of those to reload and one to jump. I've never felt the need to remap in a Zelda game, but after feeling the need to do so with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2, I might do so going forward.

It has been revealed that if you, like me, struggle to comfortably steer the new free camera while running through hallways, towns, dungeons, and, yes, Hyrule Field, you might want to consider remapping your controller. As you can see in the above image, the placement of Jump and Dash on the face buttons can make it difficult to simultaneously control the camera and sprint. This isn't typically a problem in most modern games, as clicking the right stick is often a toggle to sprint, but in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2, you need to hold the button.

If you have the Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller, copying one button's functionality to the buttons on the back of the controller is simple. All you need to do is hold the Home button on the Switch 2 Pro Controller for a moment until the Switch 2 system menu appears on the right side. Along with Power Options and any Bluetooth audio devices you have available, there is also the option to map GL and GR, the controller's back buttons on the left and right, respectively.

Sources indicate that navigate down the menu to the GL and GR, then select which one you'd like to map. It will ask you which button you want to assign to the one you selected. Everyone can choose whatever makes sense in their own head, but mapping A (Roll and Dash) to GL and X (Jump) to GR made the most sense to me. Now, while I'm using the Switch 2 Pro Controller, I can use my middle finger to hold the GL button to Dash around without removing my thumb from the camera-controlling right stick.

It has been revealed that and the best part is that, since you're not removing the functionality of the A or X buttons, you can still use them when it makes sense. For example, A also controls actions like opening up a treasure chest or door, and in my head, that feels like a face-button action, whereas rolling and dashing feel right mapped to the back buttons. The only downside is that, since this functionality is newly introduced for Switch 2 Pro Controllers, it isn't available if you're using the Joy-Cons or a Switch 1 Pro Controller. Also, it can make switching over to handheld mode challenging, as you don't have access to the back buttons in that play style.

Sources indicate that even if you don't have the ability to take advantage of this tip, either because you don't own a Switch 2 Pro Controller or because you prefer playing in handheld mode, you should still absolutely play the Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. To learn more about the experience and why it's a must-play, head to our review.

Driven: 2028 Mercedes-Benz GLA EV Is Both Familiar and a First
