💡 Key Takeaways
  • At the debut of the redesigned Mercedes-Benz GLA, firm chairman Ola Källenius said, “The ICE [internal-combustion engine] world and the BEV [battery-electric vehicle] world have come together.” And that’s true: Apart from their grilles, the gas-engine GLA and the first-ever GLA EV are virtually indistinguishable from each other.
  • Electric-first is also the go-to-market strategy—at least in Europe.
  • See all results for new 2028 Mercedes-Benz GLA-Class EV for sale near 28217.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At the debut of the redesigned Mercedes-Benz GLA, firm chairman Ola Källenius said, “The ICE [internal-combustion engine] world and the BEV [battery-electric vehicle] world have come together.” And that’s true: Apart from their grilles, the gas-engine GLA and the first-ever GLA EV are virtually indistinguishable from each other. Källenius described the design of the newly introduced GLA as “clearly electric-first,” so it’s perhaps appropriate that the EV version is the first one we’re driving.

Electric-first is also the go-to-market strategy—at least in Europe. It was to be in the U.S., too, but there’s been a reversal; we’re now slated to get the GLA hybrid first. Really, though, we won’t be getting either one for a while. We’re told to expect the gas-engine GLA sometime late next year, while the EV won’t arrive until the first half of 2028. Our recent drive of the electric GLA in Spain, therefore, was an extra-long-lead preview.

See all results for new 2028 Mercedes-Benz GLA-Class EV for sale near 28217.

It has been revealed that we’d say that gives buyers plenty of time to warm up to the newly introduced styling, except that the look is not all that different from the current GLA. More substantial, maybe: The body is bigger, sitting astride a wheelbase that is stretched 2.4 inches. The new GLA is also longer, lower, and wider.

The GLA EV is also adorned with more three-pointed stars, though not to the extent of some other recent Mercedes products. Besides the illuminated logo on the flat-panel “grille,” there’s a large badge on the rear liftgate, and the motif also appears in the headlights and taillights. Opt for Sky Control for the standard glass roof panel, and 172 light-up stars appear on the glass, which is electronically dimmable in sections.

In a recent development, the dash is lifted straight from the GLA’s sedan sibling, the CLA. As in other Benz models, there’s an available Superscreen that adds a 14.0-inch passenger display to the standard 14.0-inch center touchscreen and 10.3-inch instrument screen. With it, virtually the entire dashboard is given over to digital real estate. Sadly, almost none of the space contains any physical switchgear, although at least we still get air vents that can be aimed by hand. Wireless smartphone mirroring is standard, but a wireless charging pad costs extra. The navigation uses Google Maps and optionally offers Benz’s augmented reality, an inset showing a forward-camera view with overlaid arrows indicating direction. Unfortunately, that inset appears on the left side of the touchscreen, where it’s obscured by the driver’s right hand on the wheel; you have to peer around to see it.

Industry observers note that the on-screen climate controls are another ergonomic fail, as the touch points to change the temperature are tiny, and you have to open the climate menu to adjust the fan speed. You could ask for help from Benz’s digital assistant, which lurks within the screen, always listening. And there’s a camera trained on the driver, which can use facial recognition to automatically call up the driver’s profile and saved preferences. It can also take selfies! In a more worthwhile use of technology, buyers can purchase dash-cam functionality for the forward-facing camera.

See all results for upcoming 2028 Mercedes-Benz GLA-Class EV for sale near 28217.

Recent findings suggest that beyond the digital, the interior features high-back front seats that are firmly padded and well shaped. The high center console makes for a somewhat confining feel up front, but its floating design creates a large open bay underneath for storage. The rear-seat area boasts a flat floor and is much roomier than in the CLA sedan. The cargo hold is 15 cubic feet, expandable to 49 cubes with the rear seatbacks folded. There’s also a frunk that’s about the size of a carry-on suitcase.

The powertrains mirror the CLA EV’s. There’s a single-motor GLA250+ that sends 268 horsepower to the rear wheels. The dual-motor GLA350 4Matic has all-wheel drive and 349 horses. Both employ a two-speed transmission on the rear axle for improved efficiency at highway speeds.

In a recent development, the standard suspension has passive dampers, but the cars we drove had the optional adaptive dampers and rode on 20-inch wheels (18s are standard; 19s are also available). The smooth pavement of Barcelona and sunny coastal environs gave the dampers little to adapt to—any real assessment of the GLA’s ride quality will have to wait until we drive one on the meaner streets back home. However, the suspension acquitted itself well on our drive route’s long series of hillside curves. The GLA is composed but would be more confidence-inspiring if the steering weren’t so light and remote.

The GLA isn’t a hot hatch, though; it’s more of an urban runabout. In that context, the 268-hp GLA250+ is adequately peppy, even though Mercedes posits a rather languid 60-mph time of 7.2 seconds. We expect it to do better than that, as the CLA250+ we tested managed a 5.8-second result. The dual-motor GLA350 felt much more energetic, particularly outside of urban environs, where it swiftly passed dawdlers on two-lane roads and merged easily onto the freeway. For the GLA350, Mercedes claims a 5.3-second 60-mph time, but again that’s likely an undersell; testing a mechanically identical CLA350, we got 4.3 seconds. Even so, there are quicker EVs in this class, but one positive here is that even the higher-horsepower dual-motor version doesn’t feel like its output overwhelms its chassis—often an issue with high-horsepower EVs. Besides the standard drive modes of Eco, Comfort, Sport, and Individual, the dual-motor GLA adds a Terrain mode that optimizes the powertrain for loose surfaces; its camera system is able to stitch together a “transparent hood” view of what’s immediately in front of the car.

Recent findings suggest that when it comes time for slowing, there are three levels of liftoff regen (D, D+, and D-), as well as an Auto setting that varies the regen level based on info from the navigation system and the forward-facing cameras. Our preference is D-, which is essentially coasting, but D+ will please fans of one-pedal driving. We also tried the automated parking function, which was able to back into and out of a parallel-parking spot without trying our patience. It’s a digital add-on that’s purchased for a set time period; the same goes for the MBUX Entertainment package of multimedia streaming and app downloads.

Like the CLA EV sedan, the GLA is built on Benz’s MMA platform, with an 800-volt architecture and an 85-kWh battery. That architecture allows for speedy DC recharging, up to 320 kilowatts. Should you find a power source robust enough to reach that figure, Mercedes states the GLA battery can go from 10 percent to 80 percent in 22 minutes. (In our testing of the CLA250+ with the same hardware, it went from 10 to 80 percent in just 21 minutes.) EPA range estimates for the GLA aren’t yet available, but the CLA offers a clue, and its impressive range figures run from 312 miles on the low end to as high as 374 miles.

According to recent reports, if the GLA ends up with numbers like those, it’ll look pretty good against the electric Mini Countryman, Genesis GV60, and Cadillac Optiq, and similar-ish to a Rivian R2. Those look to be the GLA EV’s prime competitors at a base-price guesstimate of around $50K. But the EV landscape could shift significantly by the time the GLA gets here. After all, a lot can happen between now and 2028.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bilibili Gaming beat Gen.G in Brooklyn to win the 2026 League of Legends World Championship, the LPL's first world title since 2021. Added to their First Stand trophy, the result gives a Chinese side a double that no team had managed since 2016, just as Riot takes the 2027 season opener to China.

Sources indicate that bilibili Gaming are world champions. The LPL side needed four games to beat Gen.G in Latest York and win the club’s first Worlds title. The result ends a run of four straight LCK world titles. It also gives the LPL its first world crown since EDward Gaming won in 2021.

Recent findings suggest that BLG took the hardest possible route. They knocked out all four LCK teams at the event: Hanwha Life Esports, Dplus KIA, T1 and Gen.G. Every Korean side that travelled to the tournament went home after facing them.

In a recent development, the final turned early. BLG levelled the series at 1-1 by winning a 53-minute second game. It was the longest game of the whole tournament. Gen.G had reached the final with two 3-0 knockout wins, over LYON on 4 November and Invictus Gaming on 7 November.

Sources indicate that for Knight, the MVP award closes a loop. The BLG mid laner lost the 2024 final to T1. Two years later, he finished on the winning side.

It has been revealed that the runners-up looked inward after the defeat. At Gen.G’s post-final press conference, Chovy said the team had broken its own rules. Duro, playing his first Worlds, regretted that they had dropped their drafting initiative.

Industry observers note that gen.G still leave with US$800,000 as runners-up. Semi-finalists T1 and Invictus Gaming received US$400,000 each. Riot ran the event from 15 October to 14 November with 19 teams.

Sources indicate that gen.G’s admission points to the draft as a weak spot. The figures support a narrower reading too. Gen.G swept both knockout opponents before the final. Against BLG, they could not hold the lead after taking the opening game.

It has been revealed that worlds was BLG’s second international trophy of the year. In March they won the First Stand Tournament in São Paulo. They beat G2 Esports 3-1 in that final and collected the US$250,000 top prize.

Winning both events makes BLG the first team since SK Telecom T1 in 2016 to take more than one major international title in a year.

Our first Summoner’s Cup. It’s finally coming home.

To everyone who’s ever worn the jersey, worked behind the scenes, or cheered us on: we did it!#BLGWIN #Worlds2026 pic.twitter.com/E2TIgNfhgv.

— Bilibili Gaming (@BilibiliGaming) November 15, 2026.

The calendar also tilts towards China. First Stand will open the 2027 season as First Stand: All In, a one-off expanded event. Riot calls it the largest tournament it has ever produced. The event was first revealed for Southeast Asia. That region will now host First Stand in 2028 instead.

The 2027 Mid-Season Invitational will be held in Valencia.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Presumably as a way of marching ever forward towards its (alleged) 100 million player goal for Battlefield 6, EA has announced that the multiplayer shooter will be getting its first free trial later this month.
  • Industry observers note that this is, of course, specifically for players to sample the core, paid component of the game, as the recently launched Redsec remains free-to-play.
  • The Battlefield 6 trial arrives next Tuesday, November 25.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Presumably as a way of marching ever forward towards its (alleged) 100 million player goal for Battlefield 6, EA has announced that the multiplayer shooter will be getting its first free trial later this month.

Industry observers note that this is, of course, specifically for players to sample the core, paid component of the game, as the recently launched Redsec remains free-to-play. Redsec, however, offers modes like battle royale and Gauntlet, which aren’t quite the traditional Battlefield experience.

The Battlefield 6 trial arrives next Tuesday, November 25. It will run for one week, ending the following Tuesday, December 2. The trial will be available on all platforms, but won’t include all content from the full game.

According to recent reports, instead, players will have access to three of the game’s maps and five of its modes. Siege of Cairo will be there alongside Season 1’s two upcoming maps: Eastwood, and Blackwell Fields. It’s not the strongest line-up of maps, considering Eastwood is already cut from the larger Fort Lyndon battle royale map that Redsec players should be quite familiar with, but it’s something.

Sources indicate that as for modes, you can pick from Conquest, Breakthrough, Sabotage, and Team Deathmatch. Battlefield Studios didn’t say what the fifth mode is going to be, but a dedicated blog post with more information is set to arrive next week.

In a recent development, beyond the trial's content itself, the timing is certainly great. Battlefield 6 just received one of its biggest patches, kicking off the second phase of its first season. So far this season, we’ve seen two fresh maps, several new weapons - but more importantly, solutions to problems the game’s had since launch, as well as fixes to longstanding bugs.

The miserable XP progression Battlefield 6 launched with is far more tolerable. Challenges and Assignments are much easier to understand and actually finish. The often maligned weapon dispersion has been toned down. Some of the wildest vehicle bugs have been fixed. And Portal has a host of experiences that go beyond just bot farms.

In essence, Battlefield 6 feels like its reached its 1.0 status, which makes this a great entry point for new players, even if the trial could've used more of the game's better maps.

Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto 6 has a wide variety of encounters that can crop up across its central locales. While most are tied to a specific area or mission, some of the game’s most memorable are those that can occur anywhere within a given zone, adding tons of random madness to Leonida while free-roaming.

In a recent development, many of these quests are direct references to other pieces of crime fiction, from subtle hints to straight-up placing the protagonists in the situation from the films. One such quest sees either Jason or Lucia held at gunpoint by a stand-in for Tom Cruise’s character from Collateral. If you want to trigger this event and get out alive, make sure to read on!

This encounter is a standout, not appearing anywhere on the map and not being accessible until midway into Chapter 3. Once you’ve gained easy access to Vice City and start heading toward Vice Beach, sitting in any car alone for an extended period gives a suited stranger a chance to enter the back seat suddenly.

Industry observers note that he’ll proceed to stick up the protagonist, forcing them to start driving. From here on, failure to comply with his orders will lead to him shooting the player, not enough to kill outright, but enough to push you over the edge if you’re already wounded.

Your next task is to run a red light, any red light you can find. Thankfully, the agent is rather patient as long as he can tell you’re looking for a light or waiting for one to change. Once it’s clear you can follow instructions, he’ll mark an area near the park in Vice Beach for you to drive to, a trek depending on where you started the mission.

Make sure you don’t slow down too much or try to turn on the radio. Your passenger wants a nice, quiet ride to his destination. Once you arrive, things change fast, giving you a split-second decision.

Once you arrive at the location, the agent will explain that this entire charade was to put the protagonist’s face and car on a police suspect database for running that red light. Now that you’ve made it to his destination, we’re about to be in real hot water, as he guns down a nearby guard protecting a small drug lab.

Sources indicate that he insists you leave, but if you’re feeling spiteful or profit-focused, you can easily follow him inside. Without a gun to your head, he’s as easy to take down as any other enemy, plus he’ll have already cleared the guards inside and outside the lab.

Recent findings suggest that make sure to keep your car running by double-tapping your exit button, and promptly pocket everything he stood to gain before heading out. He wasn’t kidding, the cops are already on their way, so whether you’re willing to snag some for yourself or just want to hightail it, make sure you leave fast.

I’d fully recommend hitting the lab, as it’s easily a 10k payout for very little effort. There are also a few handy guns to pocket if you need the hardware. The Jeep parked outside sells for a pretty penny as well, giving you an excuse to swing by Randy and continue his questline.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Subaru vehicles are known for their dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) capabilities, but to cut costs, the manufacturer is now offering front-wheel-drive (FWD) versions on select electric models.
  • The Uncharted EV went on sale earlier this year as a smaller, sportier entry-level electric crossover positioned below the Solterra.
  • It was also the first Subaru model in about 30 years not to come with standard all-wheel drive.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Subaru vehicles are known for their dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) capabilities, but to cut costs, the manufacturer is now offering front-wheel-drive (FWD) versions on select electric models.

The Uncharted EV went on sale earlier this year as a smaller, sportier entry-level electric crossover positioned below the Solterra.

It was also the first Subaru model in about 30 years not to come with standard all-wheel drive. After unveiling the Uncharted EV last summer, Subaru remarked, “For buyers focused on affordability and range, the entry-level Uncharted Premium FWD model will be offered in limited numbers.”.

In a recent development, apparently, it wasn’t too limited. The 2027 Uncharted EV is now on sale, still with the base Premium FWD model equipped with a single 221-horsepower front-mounted electric motor.

Higher-priced Uncharted trims, including the Sport and GT, are upgraded with Subaru’s Symmetrical All-Wheel Drive system with X-Mode, delivering a combined 338 horsepower.

The 2027 Subaru Uncharted EV Premium FWD starts at $34,995, while the Sport and GT are priced from $39,795 and $43,795, respectively.

In the US, the 2027 Solterra and larger Trailseeker are still equipped with standard AWD, but Subaru is introducing newly introduced FWD (4×2) variants in some markets at a lower price point.

In comparison, the 2027 Subaru Solterra and Trailseeker EV start at $38,495 and $39,995, respectively.

Subaru opened preorders for its newly introduced 2027 electric range in Spain, including the Unchartered, Solterra, and E-Outback, which is sold as the Trailseeker in the US.

All of which will be available with a lower-priced FWD variant. Like the Uncharted, Subaru will still offer AWD on higher-priced Solterra and E-Outback trims.

The newly introduced Subaru Uncharted (4×2) starts at €26,525 ($28,900), the Solterra (4×2) starts at €35,025 ($38,200), and the E-Outback (4×2) starts at €36,525 ($39,800) in Spain, including subsidies, discounts, and other incentives.

Preorders are open for the Uncharted, while the Solterra and E-Outback are expected to launch in mid-2027.

According to recent reports, will Subaru expand FWD (4×2) to other vehicles and markets, like the US? The Uncharted is still Subaru’s only EV sold with standard FWD. The 2027 Solterra and Trailseeker are equipped with AWD and X-Mode.

How does offering a FWD option constitute "dropping" AWD?

Industry observers note that subaru's unique selling point used to be AWD available in a sedan or wagon package. Until the early 2000s, that wasn't really a possibility--after which more and relatively smaller vehicles got the option. Point being: it's not really a unique selling point anymore.

Sources indicate that more recently they've differentiated by their offroad styling and trail-readiness, e.g. better clearance, and (checks notes) the Uncharted clearance is no different than the bZ4x, and less than the bZ Woodland.

They're going to have to differentiate themselves on something else regardless.

I think it's good to see more affordable options.

AWD has become something people think they need, but almost never do, particularly with the excellent traction control of most EVs. The necessity of AWD is (largely, but not entirely) a holdover from the 90s, when traction control was not found on most vehicles.

Subaru is already selling considerably more EVs in the US, with three affordable, practical electric SUVs: the Uncharted, Solterra, and Trailseeker.

In Spring 2027, it will add its first three-row electric SUV, the Getaway. It wouldn’t be a surprise to see Subaru introduce a FWD option for other models, like the Solterra, at a lower price point.

Recent findings suggest that then again, AWD is used significantly more in the US than in Spain and other markets. For now, the Uncharted remains Subaru’s sole FWD model.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the work to continue streamlining Challenges in Battlefield 6 is clearly not done.
  • This latest round includes far fewer tweaks, but quite surprisingly, it also removes a few of the more annoying ones from the game.
  • The updated list, which Battlefield shared on Twitter, includes changes to the dreaded Recon 2 headshots beyond 150m Challenge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the work to continue streamlining Challenges in Battlefield 6 is clearly not done. Having just released a new patch - which already included several updates to Challenges and Assignments - Battlefield Studios has gone in and made even more changes.

This latest round includes far fewer tweaks, but quite surprisingly, it also removes a few of the more annoying ones from the game.

The updated list, which Battlefield shared on Twitter, includes changes to the dreaded Recon 2 headshots beyond 150m Challenge. Now, any headshot beyond 75m will count. Recon Expert 3 is another headshot-themed one that’s been updated, and now requires getting headshot kills beyond 125m, rather than the practically impossible beyond 200m that it required previously.

It has been revealed that the Rapid Fire 2 Challenge, which required getting kills beyond 50m with Assault Rifles, has been changed so it now tracks anything beyond 40m. The painful ‘Inflict damage under 15m while hip-firing with Assault Rifles’ has been entirely replaced with one that requires - the far more sensible - inflicting damage while in ADS with Assault Rifles.

A couple of Challenges, such as the one that required suppressing enemies with LMGs, and another that wanted you to deal damage to laser-designated vehicles using lock-on weapons, have both been removed.

The journey to make Challenges and Assignments easier to complete has been a long one. Progression has been one of the key areas of criticism Battlefield 6 received at launch. The glitch encompassed more than just slow player and weapon XP earn rates, it also prevented players from accessing new Training Paths for the various classes, and several of the game's weapons.

Battlefield Studios attacked the problem from multiple angles, initially boosting the XP players and their weapons would earn, before later reducing the requirements of the Challenges themselves. The developer continued to streamline those requirements over multiple patches, including majorly overhauling the system earlier this month.

It seems the studio is more confident than ever in the game, as it recently announced that Battlefield 6 will be getting its first free trial next week, offering players who do not own the full game access to iconic modes like Conquest, and Breakthrough - though on an unusual selection of maps.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, arc Raiders has received a fresh update today that’s almost entirely dedicated to balance and economy tweaks.
  • Stella Montis is available for players who’ve put in a decent number of rounds, and its close-quarters, enclosed environments have essentially turned it into the newly introduced “PvP map”, where constant action can be found.
  • That, of course, also means that the map has exposed a few balance complications with some of the game’s weapons and tools.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, arc Raiders has received a fresh update today that’s almost entirely dedicated to balance and economy tweaks. Patch 1.3.0 arrived earlier across all platforms, coming in at just under 1GB. This is an especially interesting patch because many of the changes it makes can be seen as a response to player behaviour on Stella Montis, the game’s latest map, which just joined the roster last week.

Stella Montis is available for players who’ve put in a decent number of rounds, and its close-quarters, enclosed environments have essentially turned it into the newly introduced “PvP map”, where constant action can be found.

That, of course, also means that the map has exposed a few balance complications with some of the game’s weapons and tools. Case in point: the Venator, a pistol that saw a lot of use recently. The weapon is especially powerful when fully-upgraded, something Arc Raiders developer Embark said pushed it beyond what had been originally intended.

In today’s revision, the Venator's fire rate is the thing getting hit the hardest, with each upgrade now offering slower gains to the weapon's rate-of-fire compared to the way things were. The weapon’s weight is also being increased to five from two.

Recent findings suggest that another powerful item players have been getting a lot of mileage out of recently has been the Deadline mine. Unlike the Venator, the Deadline is mainly a threat to Arc enemies, and it’s proven incredibly powerful against the largest and most fearsome, such as the Bastion, and Leaper. In fact, the mine was considered essential when taking down a Queen.

The patch vastly increases its purchase price, and makes it more difficult to craft by upping the amount each of its components requires. Perhaps the most effective nerf, however, is the reduction to the Deadline’s stock at traders from three to just one, which means you’re going to be seeing a lot less of it topside.

According to recent reports, beyond those specific changes, Embark has also tweaked explosive damage across the board. According to the developer, explosive damage was being applied to multiple parts at once, which trivialised some encounters.

This change mainly affects larger Arc units, such as the Bastion, allowing them to withstand more explosive damage before bits start coming off of them. The Hullcracker, one of the best explosive damage weapons, has also caught a nerf as part of that.

According to recent reports, check the official blog for the full change log for patch 1.3.0. If you’re just getting started with the hottest extraction shooter ever, our Arc Raiders tips offer plenty of help. You should also learn what all the different Map Conditions do in Arc Raiders, and how to best make use of each of them.

10 Best Food Centric Video Games

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1413 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that for many countries across the globe, 2026’s holiday season is just around the corner.
  • While some people may be stressing out about the prospect of cooking so many dishes for the holiday season, there’s likely just as many people out there who not only enjoy tasting all kinds of meals but enjoy preparing them for friends and family alike as well.
  • For those who love cooking and all things food-related, here’s a look at the 10 best food centric video games people can enjoy playing through, whether solo or with friends, in between tantalizing holiday meals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that for many countries across the globe, 2026’s holiday season is just around the corner. With those holidays come celebratory family gatherings full of all kinds of delicious food to eat.

While some people may be stressing out about the prospect of cooking so many dishes for the holiday season, there’s likely just as many people out there who not only enjoy tasting all kinds of meals but enjoy preparing them for friends and family alike as well.

For those who love cooking and all things food-related, here’s a look at the 10 best food centric video games people can enjoy playing through, whether solo or with friends, in between tantalizing holiday meals.

For a few decades now, food companies have occasionally released tie-in video games often referred to as advergames, in wacky attempts to attract gamers to purchase their products. While Burger King has released a few advergames over the years, its best was arguably Sneak King.

One of three BK games for the original Xbox and Xbox 360, Sneak King is a third-person stealth game following the fast-food chain’s now-retired Burger King mascot, as he sneaks around various locations to surprise deliver BK meals such as omelet sandwiches, hash browns, and more.

While Sneak King didn’t have a lot of depth to it, the game did represent the often wacky yet creative game design the sixth and seventh console generations are remembered for.

Anybody who grew up owning an iPod Touch, iPad, or iPhone in the early 2010s likely played some of the most iconic mobile apps of all time, such as Angry Birds, Doodle Jump, and the subject for this entry, Halfbrick Studios’ Fruit Ninja.

The premise for Fruit Ninja is simple: players must use a touch screen, VR controllers, or their own hands (in the case of the Kinect versions) to equip ninja blades and slice up as much flying fruit as possible without hitting flying bombs.

Fruit Ninja is an easy game for sure, but it’s one that endlessly fun no matter what form or mode it’s played in, whether it be the Xbox 360 Kinect version, the Fruit Ninja FX version found at Dave & Buster's and other arcades, or the latest version on Nex Playground.

J. R. R. Tolkien’s The Lord of the Rings franchise is beloved for many reasons, such as its mythology, character arcs, and fantastical creatures. Another aspect of the franchise many people adore is the calm, joyful culture of Hobbit life.

Numerous LOTR fans strive to live life as merrily as the Shire’s inhabitants, and one way people can do so is by playing the life simulation game Tales of the Shire: A The Lord of the Rings Game, set after The Hobbit but before The Fellowship of the Ring.

Here, players can create their own Hobbit as they complete tasks such as farming, fishing, and decorating Hobbit-holes in the emerging Hobbiton village of Bywater. Most importantly for this article, they can also cook a variety of dishes for their Hobbit neighbors.

Industry observers note that in 2006, Nintendo helped many young gamers get interested in cooking for the first time by releasing the minigame compilation Cooking Mama on the Nintendo DS. While that game is fantastic, many Nintendo players would consider Cooking Mama 5: Bon Appétit! to be the best entry in the CM series.

The final mainline entry in the CM series, Cooking Mama 5: Bon Appétit! Features similar modes and overall gameplay to its predecessors, but introduces many new minigames and recipes such as Pumpkin Gratin, Hawaiian Pancakes, and Herb Hotdogs.

Players could even manage a burger shop, take care of pet fish, customize kitchen designs, and gather ingredients from plants, with each action feeling more precise thanks to the 3DS’ improved stylus controls.

Video games have let people play as medieval heroes, monsters, space marines, and more, but one unique game did the impossible by making playing as actual food fun. That game was Bossa Studios’ I Am Bread.

Set in the same universe as Surgeon Simulator, I Am Bread has players control a singular piece of bread as it strives to move about various locations such as a kitchen and a bathroom in an effort to become toast, whilst struggling to maintain its edibility by avoiding the ground, bugs, and other contaminants.

While the premise of I Am Bread might sound ridiculous at first, it actually winds up being a fairly hilarious, challenging, and rewarding game, with all of the crazy antics and chaos the slices of bread get into.

Recent findings suggest that people love parties, candy, and piñatas, but only one game developer has dared tackling the question of how piñatas are made. As seen in Rare’s classic life simulation game Viva Piñata.

Set on the initially ruinous Pinata island, Viva Piñata has players restore a garden on the island with the goal of attracting, domesticating, breeding, and defending local piñata wildlife, so that they can eventually be sent out to parties across the globe full of delicious candy.

Viva Piñata may be 20 years old at this point, but it’s still just as fun and colorful as ever, whether people play it on Xbox 360, PC, or via the Rare Replay compilation.

Industry observers note that the Illinois-based game developer Young Horses is famous for its Octodad series, which itself could be considered a food centric game since a chef chases Octodad around. However, the team wound up making one of the most creative food centric games yet in 2020, with Bugsnax.

Here, people play as a muppet-like Grumpus newspaper journalist, as they set out to Snaktooth Island to document the food-like Bugsnax creatures living there only to get caught up in a mysterious conspiracy surrounding the island and its inhabitants.

Industry observers note that for anyone who wanted to explore the living food island of Swallow Falls in Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs 2, Bugsnax is the game for you. You can encounter all kinds of food-inspired wildlife on Snaktooth Island, such as the elephant cheeseburger Bunger and the crab apple Crapple.

In a recent development, many of the best food centric games were released years or even decades ago, but one latest 2026 title has quickly become a favorite among food fanatics. That game being the anime-inspired cooking and restaurant management simulator KuloNiku: Bowl Up!

According to recent reports, the 13th game released by Gambir Studio, KuloNiku: Bowl Up! has players inherit their grandmother’s once-famous meatball restaurant in the cozy town of KuloNiku. They set out to restore it to its former glory by experimenting with new recipes, decor, and competing with other chefs in Meatball Brawls.

People aren’t just making simple spaghetti and meatball dishes, though, as customers will often request comedically complex recipes requiring players to chop, boil, fry, and torch all kinds of ingredients, with some customers even going on to become potential friends or rivals.

Many food centric games focus on people opening up a fresh restaurant and rising to Michelin star status, but no game quite replicates that experience in such a unique and fun way like Mintrocket’s Dave the Diver.

A primarily 2D adventure and management game, Dave the Diver follows the title character as he and his friends open their Bancho Sushi Bar near a massive, mysterious Blue Hole, with Dave having to dive for fish during the day and manage the sushi restaurant at night.

Recent findings suggest that diving for fish and managing the sushi restaurant are certainly fun activities, but there's far more to Dave the Diver than initially meets the eye. Players can fight huge sea creature bosses, sing karaoke, and even interact with mermaids from the Sea People Village.

Without a doubt, the best food centric game out there is Ghost Town Games’ Overcooked! All You Can Eat, a remastered collection of Overcooked and Overcooked 2 with all DLC expansions and completely brand-fresh content.

A third-person, top-down perspective cooking game, Overcooked 1 and 2 feature teams of up to four chefs working together to serve food in an orderly, oftentimes hectic, manner from restaurants, food trucks, and unconventional locations such as a space station and icebergs.

While Overcooked may not be as realistic with its food as other games, it perfectly recreates the fun, often chaotic nature of restaurant cooking into a cartoony, co-op experience and forces people to learn to work together as a team, making it a perfect food centric game.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting latest series concurrent player records on Steam.
  • The latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’ve been paying any attention to the shooter market these past few months, you won’t be surprised to learn that Battlefield 6 has been an unprecedented success for EA, and the Battlefield series as a whole.

The game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting latest series concurrent player records on Steam. Thanks to new data, we now better understand the true scale of this launch.

The latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived. This iteration covers the month of October, which is when Battlefield 6 was released.

Battlefield 6 was the top-selling game across all platforms during October - which isn’t surprising. It has overtaken NBA 2K26 to become 2025’s best-selling game year-to-date, making it the best-selling Battlefield game ever.

In October alone, the game sold more than the lifetime sales of Battlefield 1, previously the best-selling entry in the franchise.

According to recent reports, battlefield 6 even set records beyond just its own series, having now produced the highest single-month dollar sales (physical and digital) total for any full game released in the last three years. The previous record holder was 2022’s Modern Warfare 2.

Industry observers note that november’s report, which is set to arrive midway through December, will show, once and for all, whether Battlefield 6 has been able to overtake Black Ops 7. With one exception, Call of Duty games have, for more than a decade, topped the best-selling year-to-date chart. Regardless of the quality of the individual titles, or the competition in any given year, nothing has been able to shake that dominance.

In a recent development, given all this momentum, Battlefield 6 has a shot at dethroning Call of Duty this year, beating Black Ops 7 to become the year’s best-seller. You never want to count out the sheer popularity of Call of Duty among casual players, however, which is what’s going to make December’s report all the more interesting.

In a recent development, jon Batiste has collaborated with the likes of Alicia Keys, Lenny Kravitz, Prince, Stevie Wonder, Willie Nelson, and many more. He performed the national anthem at Super Bowl LIX. He's headed up the musical efforts of The Late Show with Stephen Colbert. He's taken home more awards than we can realistically list in this article (including eight Grammys, as well as an Academy Award, a BAFTA Award, and a Golden Globe). But as I sit down with Batiste for a brief conversation about video game music, his energy transcends the Zoom call.

According to recent reports, before I can even ask a question, Batiste begins singing to greet me, then nerds out about my NBA Jam and Street Fighter II cabinets. He begins humming the menu music from NBA Jam and reminiscing about all the quarters he pumped into his local Street Fighter cabinet. The Louisiana native and Juilliard School alum has been an ardent gaming enthusiast for nearly three decades, with compositions from games like Sonic the Hedgehog and Final Fantasy VII inspiring his earliest musical endeavors. Spend enough time watching video game music performances on social media, and you'll likely soon find videos of Batiste sitting with famed Final Fantasy composer Nobuo Uematsu, or of Batiste performing gaming music.

Recent findings suggest that with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time delivering some of the most iconic music of all time (and Batiste famously loving the music), it makes sense that Nintendo would bring him out to Newly introduced York to serve as a special guest at the launch event for the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on Switch 2. I sat down with Batiste for a few minutes to chat about his love of video game music, his history with Nintendo, and why "Guile's Theme" from Street Fighter II just goes so well with everything.

According to recent reports, ocarina of Time is easily one of the most key video games ever made, and one of the things that makes it so special is the music. What about Ocarina of Time sticks out to you sonically?First off, if you want to get super inside baseball, technical music nerdery, which I love to do, in the compositions, there's a way that major chords and minor chords in... no sevenths, just root, third, fifth. They alternate, and it creates this magic that is, like, it's wistful, and it's simple. It feels ancient, and it feels like it's the music that is going on in your mind as you're generating thoughts and your imagination is churning. And the major chords are happening just after the minors in this contrary motion that's happening, so it feels like the music is going like this: It's going up – major, minor – like [sings the main Legend of Zelda theme song].

So, it's expanding and contracting, which is a musical allegory for the expansion and the openness of the world that Link is in. It's like [Koji Kondo] figured out how to capture the essence of the gameplay, but also the essence of magic and simplicity, which I think is really what makes... that's the music's power! So, you could listen to the music in the game, and you could also listen to it apart from the game and experience that magic.

Are there any tracks in Ocarina of Time that stand out to you as the most musically sophisticated or compositionally impressive?Oh man. Well, I think of it as a suite, so that's what makes it actually... there's nothing that's more or less complex, but the thought to figure out how to make all of the themes be interrelated yet singular. "Song of Storms" is, like, for me, that's a personal favorite. That's why I like to play it. I like to play a lot of the themes. That's how I grew up! I would play the game, and then, I would go to an instrument. Once we played for hours on Nintendo, we'd go and play Nintendo on piano! It was like a trade-off there, you know? I've been doing this since I was about 11 years old.

Recent findings suggest that taking it back to that 11-year-old Jon, talk to me a little bit about your history in general.Okay, so my history with Nintendo goes back to the NES. Christmas morning. Duck Hunt. You remember that? Maybe the first game I ever played. No, the first game I ever played was Donkey Kong, and then Duck Hunt, and then Super Mario Bros. Staples! We're talking about the early '90s. We had a room where I would go – it was my domain – and we had this blue shag carpet, and I would sit back there, and I would basically disappear into the carpet playing Nintendo for hours and hours.

And my mind is kind of... my mind can become a spiral; it can become a tornado. And I realized even then that going into this world of the game, even if I didn't win – it's not about winning or losing – it helps to organize the spiral of my mind and give me ideas and inspiration. So then, I started to get into Street Fighter II when I started to play more communally with my sister and my cousins. Yoko Shimomura, who I also had the pleasure of meeting and collaborating with, she composed incredible themes for each character, and that's when I really started to get a true love for fighting games.

And then, we would play so many of the Street Fighter franchise. We would play a lot of Final Fight. There were so many things... there was Double Dragon, then we got Mega Man... all these different series. Mega Man X is [an] all-time favorite. And then, here comes The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and that sort of expands the canon while also blending all of the elements: score, combat, the sort of linear quality of, like, a Donkey Kong or Super Mario World, and expanding the world in that way, expanding the canon in that way. Mind-blowing! So,  that sort of solidified my palate in terms of my favorite type of game.

You mentioned Street Fighter II. There's a meme about "Guile's Theme" and how it goes with everything. What about that composition makes it so it has the ability to enhance whatever video you pair it with?Wow! So, it has momentum in a way that is extremely [sings the melody of "Guile's Theme"] ... It draws you in, which is what you want [with] anything that you're starting when you're commencing a journey or watching something. You want it to draw you in, and that kind of pulls you in as that call and response. But it's an immediate announcement with the brass, and then the bass call and response. So, it's automatically giving you this feeling that something's happening, and I've got to pay attention to it! So that's the first step right there. And the tempo is really... it's a great tempo! It almost has the feeling of the great themes from, like, an '80s protagonist that's in a fighting movie. I think that was kind of the archetype. Yoko was probably drawing from that archetype, right? The action-hero archetype.

Porsche is transforming its current lineup of luxury SUVs and sports cars into a veritable stampede of electrified steeds. Before the gas-powered 718 Cayman and 718 Boxster bid farewell, Porsche intends to debut an all-electric 718 EV that's rumored to be available in both hardtop and convertible variants. Few details are available beyond confirmation of its existence, but Porsche did say the electric 718 will ride on a newly developed sports-car platform that works to keep the vehicle as light as possible. Expect a rear-motor-only version to serve as the entry-level 718 EV, while an all-electric GTS equivalent will likely use all-wheel drive to provide additional grip and even brisker acceleration. The 718 EV should have at least 250 miles of driving range, and will likely use a similar 800-volt architecture that allows the large Taycan to DC fast-charge at a rate of up to 270 kWh. We'll update this space as specs become available; we expect the 718 EV to launch sometime in 2027 as a 2028 model.

Recent findings suggest that the 718 EV is likely to debut for the 2028 model year as the Porsche's third electric car. At a media roundtable in 2023, Porsche CEO Oliver Blume stated the all-electric sports car would replace the gas-powered 718 Cayman and Boxster. Since then, reports have come out that say that the gas-powered 718 cars would end production in mid-2025.

Sources indicate that if this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying fresh.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You’d be forgiven for not remembering PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction off-shoot of the original battle royale shooter, PUBG. Black Budget has been sort of floating around the internet for months, but Krafton never really committed to revealing core details about the game, or when players will actually get to play it.

This changes today, as the publisher - along with the game’s developer, PUBG Studios, have finally lifted the lid off the upcoming shooter.

Black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter. Squads of players infiltrate a mysterious island trapped in a time loop. There’s a bit of a STALKER element here with anomalies and various, unpredictable environmental shifts.

Coli, the island in question, hides a research facility that holds secrets and artefacts, which is what players will be attempting to extract. This is very much a PvPvE shooter, though PUBG Studios says the focus will be on exploration and discovery, rather than constant combat.

It has been revealed that the game’s first set of closed alpha tests is set for December. The first takes place December 12-14, and another is scheduled for December 19-21. That’s six days across two weeks, with the test only being available on PC. Both sessions will be open to players in North America, Europe, and Asia.

Industry observers note that as it usually works with these sorts of tets on Steam, the game’s Steam page has a link where you can request access. If granted, you’ll be able to find the closed alpha in your library and download it when the time comes.

Recent findings suggest that though this is a closed test, Krafton confirmed that players will be able to capture and livestream their gameplay. In fact, watching content creators might be how you get access, as Black Budget is going to have a Twitch Drops event running alongside those sessions.

When I played Arc Raiders prior to its launch, I likened its tense and uncertain atmosphere to that of the early days of PUBG, so it’s going to be very interesting to see what actual PUBG does with the extraction shooter premise.

It has been revealed that so far, it sounds like it’s going to be doing its own thing, leaning more into the adventure side of the subgenre, but we’ll have to see how it all shakes out when the tests start. Indeed, the BR-like constantly shrinking circle sounds like it could be a game-changing twist.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Red Dog Mine in Alaska burns about 40,000 gallons of diesel a day to keep one of the world’s largest zinc mines running, and now, an 8.8-megawatt (MW) solar farm and battery storage will help cut that fuel use.
  • According to recent reports, the Alaska Energy Authority’s board unanimously approved a nearly $5 million loan for the project through its Power Project Fund.
  • Red Dog sits about 105 miles north of the Arctic Circle, on land owned by NANA, an Iñupiat-owned Alaska Native corporation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Red Dog Mine in Alaska burns about 40,000 gallons of diesel a day to keep one of the world’s largest zinc mines running, and now, an 8.8-megawatt (MW) solar farm and battery storage will help cut that fuel use.

According to recent reports, the Alaska Energy Authority’s board unanimously approved a nearly $5 million loan for the project through its Power Project Fund. Tugliq Red Dog1 will build, own, and operate the roughly $35 million solar project and sell the electricity to mine operator Teck Alaska. The state’s loan review states site work began in June and expects the solar and storage to come online in October 2028.

Red Dog sits about 105 miles north of the Arctic Circle, on land owned by NANA, an Iñupiat-owned Alaska Native corporation. The array would be larger than any solar farm operating in Alaska today, as KOTZ’s Desiree Hagen reported for Alaska Public Media. Hagen reported that the prepares call for more than 15,000 panels across around 30 acres.

The mine gets all its power from on-site diesel generators. In summer, it can draw so much electricity that Teck has to cut power elsewhere at the site. The solar array and the 8.8 MW, 15 megawatt-hour (MWh) battery will give the operator another source of power during those crunches.

The state of Alaska expects the solar and storage project to cover about 5% of the zinc mine’s electricity needs under its current operating plan. The project could do even more after mining ends, covering about 90% of the site’s annual electricity needs.

Sources indicate that teck expects the mine’s existing deposits to support operations through 2031, and it’s studying whether to develop two nearby deposits. If that expansion goes ahead, the state projects the solar and battery project would cover about 3% of the larger operation’s electricity needs. If mining ends, demand will drop sharply, but the site will still need electricity for cleanup and long-term water treatment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, somehow, after all these years, there are still a considerable number of vehicles equipped with Takata airbags, though their number should be considerably lower in the near future. Honda just issued a recall for 810,592 cars equipped with Takata airbags that could rupture due to propellant degradation caused by high humidity.

According to documents filed with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), the recall covers some 2013 Acura RDX, ILX, Honda CR-V, Civic, and Accord models. The affected Accords and Acuras are all from the 2013 model year, while the CR-V and Civic populations include both 2012 and 2013 vehicles.

See all results for used cars for sale near 21215.

According to recent reports, the NHTSA documents show that the affected vehicles are equipped with airbag inflators that use a phase-stabilized ammonium nitrate propellant, which is intended to control moisture within the inflator. Over time, exposure to high humidity and repeated temperature changes can cause the inflator to become brittle. When the brittle inflators are deployed, they could turn into projectiles that shoot metal fragments through the cabin, potentially injuring or killing occupants.

The recall comes after years of investigation and analysis by Honda, which was routinely shared with NHTSA. The recall documents show that on November 19, 2026, Honda determined that the inflators posed enough of a risk to warrant the new recall.

Sources indicate that owners of affected models will be contacted by mail and urged to bring their vehicle to a Honda or Acura dealership. Dealer technicians will replace the driver and passenger airbag inflators with a different model for free. Dealers have already been notified of the recall, with owner notification letters scheduled to be sent on December 18. Owners concerned that their car might be included in the recall can check on the NHTSA recalls site as well as NHTSA’s dedicated Takata airbag recall page.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the latest HoYoverse Special Program has brought us major Genshin Impact news. Version Luna 3 has been fully revealed, continuing the Nod-Krai story. The fresh chapter arrives December 3 across all platforms.

Recent findings suggest that the Moon-Prayer Night is the significant in-world festival, marking Dameselette's final night before she sets off for the moon. The newly introduced update, of course, introduces new playable characters, one with an interesting mechanic.

According to recent reports, the events of this latest chapter take place following Rarcher of Solnari’s defeat. The victory has given way to the Moon-Prayer Night celebrations, which brings various stalls to the Nasha Town, alongside a new souvenir stamp book where you can record your memories.

Recent findings suggest that all is not fine, however, as Alice and Nicole Reeyn come bearing some bad news about phantoms appearing across the Nod-Krai region at Teyvat's borders. There’s a mystery to be uncovered here, and your journey to do so won’t be a lonely one.

Sources indicate that the highly-anticipated Durin is at last the latest playable character. A 5-Star Pyro Sword wielder, Durin can switch between two different forms: one lets him deal damage, while the other is best suited to supporting the team.

Durin was once a dragon, you see, who was later given a human body. This is why he’s able to switch forms. The more powerful, Abyssal-infused form can launch major attacks on single targets to boost his own Vaporize and Melt damage, while his support form reduces enemies’ Elemental Resistance and deals AoE Pyro damage.

Durin’s Story Quest will shed more light on that aspect of his life, and completing it earns you a reward for him. Speaking of quests, completing the Archon Quest will grant you 500 Primogems. As a member of Hexenzirkel, Durin and other characters can gain newly introduced powers when you complete more quests in Moon-Prayer Night.

All characters connected to the Hexenzirkel can benefit from certain story quests tied to their abilities. It has been revealed that we have been writing a lot about The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time remake this week because it is one of 2026's most exciting games, and it's real good. The remake is not particularly surprising. It mostly sticks to the trajectory of the original game, but there is a reason it is considered one of the best games of all time. It also looks and plays amazing.

You can read the full review here (or watch the video above), but we also have a significant interview with the game's producers (one of whom worked on the original Ocarina of Time, and one who directed Breath of the Wild among many other Zelda games), some details about the Easter Eggs that did and did not make it into the remake, and a very handy tip for the game if you happen to be playing with a Switch 2 Pro controller.

World of Warcraft: Forever is out now and it’s a great time to jump into the revamped and expanded version of a project that changed online games forever back in 2004. A thousand upcoming quests, multiple new zones, countless revamps, and an impressively stunning visual overhaul make it the perfect time to jump in for anyone who’s ever been curious to explore Azeroth.

Sources indicate that 2022's Escape Academy was a sneaky little puzzle game that surprised me and its sequel released this week. Taking place in a school obsessed with puzzles, you play as a student who must make their way through a series of escape rooms. The puzzles are clever, and the setting is charming, but the secret weapon is the local, split-screen co-op. Solving puzzles together is fun especially when one player needs to look at one section of a room to help dictate a solution on the other side of the room. My wife and I both love video games, but rarely play co-op games together just because of our disparate, individual tastes. But Escape Room is one we enjoyed together and we're so far enjoying the sequel. My only complaint so far is... I wish it ran a little better.

It has been revealed that while we collectively use the term here for the sake of familiarity, I’m always a bit hesitant in my own mind to label a game under the wide banner of “Metroidvania.” In part, that’s because I think the two referenced games (Metroid and Castlevania: Symphony of the Night) are actually more different than they might appear at first glance. Gloomsoft’s recent release, Moadra, recognizes that distinction, crafting a game that draws heavy inspiration from the specific tradition of Super Metroid, even while presenting an intriguing and atmospheric fiction that is great fun to discover. In movement, actions, and exploration, Moadra feels remarkably similar to  the best of the 2D Metroid games. A scanning tool also leans into the Metroid inspirations, revealing details about the weird alien world you’re navigating. If you’ve been hungry for a game that scratches that particular itch of sci-fi gear/ability-gated exploration, I think you’ll find a lot to love in this game.

I get the Marvel fatigue we've all been experiencing. There are a lot of games and a lot of movies and a lot of TV shows and many are good, but lately most feel like homework. For those reasons, you'd be forgiven for dismissing the 2021 Guardians of the Galaxy game, but I promise you it is good. For one, it is standalone. It does not directly tie to any specific Marvel media. No homework necessary. And for two, it's just a really good game with an affecting story and a unique take on the characters that most of us met for the first time in the movies. And, for the BioWare fans out there mourning the loss of Mass Effect, this game has some Mass Effect energy. It's available on Switch 2 this week and I happily recommend it, especially if you missed it five years ago.

This exclusively two-player board game features a fun mix of activities. You act as both a dungeon architect, and an adventurer delving into said dungeons. Each player creates their own version of a challenging dungeon filled with traps, monsters, and treasures.

Sources indicate that but you’re also forced to take on the dangers of your opponent’s crafted dungeon, to see who manages to come out on top. If you have fond memories of the hidden-info nature of old games like Battleship, but you want some greater strategic depth and fantasy flavor thrown in, this one is a great pick.

While the offending image was not shared, GTA 6’s nudist areas feature a mix of fully clothed and naked NPCs roaming around, mirroring the real experiences of clothing-optional resorts that are a roaring trade in coastal Florida. The image was sent via PSN’s private message service and not posted publicly on any part of Sony’s gaming service.

Although the photo was taken with GTA 6’s in-game camera application and did not feature real-world nudity, PlayStation somehow flagged the image as pornographic and sent a message saying it breached the service’s Code of Conduct. The game’s hyper-realistic graphics might have tricked Sony’s strict auto-moderation tools that real sensitive images were being sent.

The game’s hyper-realistic graphics might have tricked Sony’s strict auto-moderation tools that real sensitive images were being sent.

The player was warned that any further infractions could lead to permanent suspension, causing him to frantically post on social media about his experience.

In their post, the player cautioned others: "Do not, I repeat, do not send any photos taken with the in-game camera across the PSN messaging network that contain nudity." The official notice from PlayStation Safety confirmed the content "breached the Code of Conduct" and cited "pornographic or obscene content.".

The ban comes as a real risk for players who share content from the game online, meaning auto-moderation tools on social media or messaging services may inadvertently restrict content featuring risque or outright obscene imagery.

While PSN flagged pornographic content, the irony comes that Sony is actively promoting Grand Theft Auto 6 on a grand scale across its platform, featuring multiple ads and promotional images that encourage players to pick the game up on PlayStation.

Sources indicate that however, Sony also has to abide with the local laws of the hundreds of countries it operates in, meaning that its auto-moderation tools must respond promptly to perceived threats or the breaking of rules to protect young and vulnerable customers from harm. Breaking: Can Pirelli’s Cyber Tyre Technology Replace Drive Modes?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (959 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Caranddriver

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, after roughly 25 years of development, Pirelli's Cyber Tyre technology is preparing for a wider rollout.
  • That information, combined with software help from Bosch, allows a vehicle to adjust its ABS and traction-control calibrations based on tire data.
  • "This is one of the worst environments for electronics," explained Pirelli chief technical officer Piero Misani.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, after roughly 25 years of development, Pirelli's Cyber Tyre technology is preparing for a wider rollout. The tires use a sensor that looks a lot like a Dexcom G7 to feed temperature, air pressure, acceleration, and identification data to a vehicle's computers.

That information, combined with software help from Bosch, allows a vehicle to adjust its ABS and traction-control calibrations based on tire data. For example, swap your summer tires for squishier winter rubber, and a compatible car could recognize the change and automatically adjust how its electronic controls intervene, leaving you free to imagine a world where maybe we all just drove better.

See all results for used cars for sale near 64850.

"This is one of the worst environments for electronics," explained Pirelli chief technical officer Piero Misani. The sensor, weighing just 13 grams, is bonded to the tire's inner liner beneath the tread using a specially developed adhesive and rubber housing. The process was developed using learnings from Pirelli's Noise Cancelling System, which uses foam inside the tire to absorb sound waves and reduce cabin vibration. The sensor must survive extreme temperatures, constant flexing, and the insane lateral g-forces that tires are susceptible to at over 200 mph. Engineers explained that its battery is designed to outlast the tire and enters a low-power sleep mode during extended storage.

Industry observers note that the more inspiring part is what the car does with the information it gathers. As we found in our recent all-weather tire comparison test, summer, winter, and all-season tires perform dramatically differently. Yet a vehicle's electronic controls are generally calibrated around its original equipment, using things like wheel speed sensors that aren’t as close to the road surface as the Cyber Tyre. Instead, it identifies the specific tire installed at each corner, allowing it to use different wheel-slip targets. And with the sensor attached to the inside of the tire, the data informing those systems is closer to the road surface than ever.

We sampled the technology at Las Vegas Motor Speedway in two Mercedes-AMG GT63 S four-doors wearing Cyber Tyre-equipped P Zero MS all-season tires.

The first exercise had us pin the throttle through a corner from 40 mph using three different traction-control calibrations, all on the same P Zero MS all-season tires. The first, intended for ultra-high-performance summer tires, was overly restrictive, cutting power before the tires could deliver much acceleration. The second, calibrated for winter tires, permitted considerably more wheelspin, making the AMG easy to slide. Despite that setting being the most fun (and our favorite), Cyber Tyre delivered a happy medium, allowing more controlled acceleration without either extreme.

See all results for used cars for sale near 64850.

In a recent development, this is where Cyber Tyre begins to make the case against selectable drive modes. The same car, wearing the same tires, just behaved three different ways without any mechanical changes. It's not going to replace the button that stiffens your dampers or changes your exhaust note, but it could eventually make some traction-related settings redundant.

According to recent reports, the second AMG demonstrated ABS braking from 65 mph. With Cyber Tyre integration active, our stopping distance improved by 0.9 meter, or about three feet, according to Pirelli's instrumentation. That's not dramatically different, but still a measurable improvement.

Of course, these demonstrations weren't proof that Cyber Tyre can outperform a conventional system already calibrated for the correct tires. And the technology isn't smart enough to know it's snowing just because the tires are cold. But the distinction is that Cyber Tyre can give the car information about its tires without the driver doing anything. That could be super useful as tires wear, temperatures change, or owners swap between summer and winter sets. Pirelli is also developing tire-wear estimates using its sensor data, which could prove useful for fleet operators managing hundreds of vehicles.

Pirelli and Bosch confirmed their development partnership in 2024, and the technology has already appeared in vehicles from McLaren and Pagani. Pirelli executives say a substantially higher-volume application should be announced in the first half of 2027, with production expected in 2028. So it's possible this tech could arrive in models as common as a Ford pickup.

In a recent development, pirelli is also investing approximately $1.2 billion to expand its Rome, Georgia, manufacturing facility, where Cyber Tyre-equipped products will be produced alongside conventional tires. By 2033, the firm expects annual production capacity to reach six million tires and prepares to add up to 1000 engineering jobs.

According to recent reports, they also recently announced that China's state-owned Sinochem, formerly Pirelli's largest shareholder, reduced its ownership to 13.6 percent in November. The Italian government has restricted Sinochem's influence and specifically prohibited sharing Cyber Tyre data with entities connected to the Chinese government. Following those governance changes, Pirelli received U.S. authorization to market the technology here. Not that anyone was worried about a Pagani Utopia Roadster being a boon of classified information.

Recent findings suggest that cyber Tyre isn't about to take the Ford Bronco's G.O.A.T. modes out back to shoot them. There are plenty of reasons to let drivers decide how their cars behave. But after experiencing three dramatically different calibrations in the same AMG, it's easy to see why some of those decisions might eventually be better left to the car. Just make sure we’re able to fully disable them.

It has been revealed that austin Irwin has worked for Car and Driver for over 10 years in various roles. He's steadily worked his way from an entry-level data entry position into driving vehicles for photography and video, and is now reviewing and testing cars. What will he do next? Who knows, but he better be fast.

Even if you don’t care about the rivalries between the top multiplayer first-person shooters series, it’s hard to ignore how much EA wanted to stick it to Call of Duty this year with Battlefield 6.

Activision saw that coming early enough that it ran multiple free weekends around major moments for EA’s game, including its launch, seemingly in an effort to capture some of those players and keep them away from BF6.

Both Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 have now launched, and though exact sales figures may never be detrmined (though EA did announce 7 million sold in the first week), it’s very clear at this point from every metric we can see that BF6 came out on top this year.

The recent Black Ops 7 launch clearly hasn’t made many people happy, so just like Activision made Black Ops 6 free to play at BF6’s launch, EA has now done the same with its own game. The Battlefield 6 free trial, which was unveiled last week, is just an hour away at the time of this writing.

This is the first trial for the core game, and it arrives some six weeks after Battlefield 6 officialy launched, and four weeks following the release of the free-to-play Battlefield Redsec, which has battle royale and other components.

Beyond all the drama surrounding the two rival shooter franchises, the Battlefield 6 trial is itself pretty straightfoward, and is notably nowhere near as genrous as some of the Call of Duty ones we’ve seen recently.

Sources indicate that the trial goes live today at 4am PT, 7am ET, 12pm GMT across all platforms, and will be available for a week; ending Tuesday, December 2. It includes three core maps: Siege of Cairo, Eastwood, and Blackwell Fields.

Industry observers note that players will have access to four game modes, played on different versions of the same maps. Conquest, Breakthrough, Sabotage, and Team Deathmatch will all be available to choose from, and there don’t appear to be any level or XP limits in the trial.

Unfortunatley, just as the free trial was about to go live, the game got hit with a major matchmaking outage that took down all matchmaking in the core game, leaving Redsec unaffected.

Hopefully EA can resolve this matter before the trial officially kicks off.

Infinity Nikki has officially evolved into a bigger, more feature-rich game. After months of waiting, version 2.0 has arrived to bring massive overhauls - and plenty of new content - to the dress-up RPG.

According to recent reports, the update, available now on all platforms, is dubbed Terra’s Call. It adds a new region, Itzaland, to the game’s world. It also reshapes the rest of Miraland.

Industry observers note that itzaland is only the tip of the iceberg. Elderwood Forest and Spira are the region's two upcoming areas, with more to be unlocked down the line. This patch also upgrades several core mechanics, including combat and exploration. There’s a suite of new traversal abilities, too, like grappling, low-gravity and even gigantification.

Recent findings suggest that archery is a fresh addition to combat, and you’ll spot new combat companions as part of the adaptive energy mechanics. Terra’s Call clearly has a focus on interactivity with the game’s world, to make it feel more alive and lived-in.

According to recent reports, there’s a host of new interactions you can have with cute creatures like singing mushrooms, and wall-climbing snails. Version 2.0 also makes for a great starting point for new players as both main and side stories are now available for free.

It wouldn’t be a dress-up game without a host of newly introduced fashion sets, and outfits, of course - and there's plenty here, both free and paid. The launch of the new enhancement also kicks off several in-game events, including some that celebrate the game’s second anniversary, and Nikki’s birthday.

Infold also recently confirmed that Idina Menzel — the actor who originated the roles of Elphaba in Wicked and Elsa in Frozen — will be singing the brand-new theme song for Version 2.0. You can listen to that on the official Infinity Nikki YouTube channel, where you can also watch a behind-the-scenes interview with Ms Menzel.

Industry observers note that tesla is rolling out the 15th iteration of its Full Self-Driving (Supervised) software, and the upgrade comes with some pretty impressive graphics. It’s called Tesla Reality View, and it’s exactly that, using the vehicle’s cameras to record what’s going on around you, then re-create the scene on the central screen accurately.

The intent is to show a visual representation of what the latest FSD driver assistance is going to do, as represented by onscreen arrows. Turns are represented, and the screen shows what parking spot the vehicle has selected when using auto park.

Recent findings suggest that it all looks extremely slick, just like the real world rendered into a video game in real time. Tesla says the actual driving assistance has also been greatly improved, with an increased ability to spot and react to potholes, small animals, and road debris. The system also uses fleet learning from the trips other Teslas take on the same route, something Tesla has been doing for several iterations of FSD.

See all results for used Tesla for sale near 77407.

Although Tesla claims that this new iteration is 25 times safer in critical interventions, this claim isn’t backed up with provided data such as miles driven; it’s just Tesla’s claim thus far.

Industry observers note that users’ experiences since the rollout have indicated that V15 appears to be more cautious in certain situations, and in some cases a little overcautious. Posts on Reddit’s Tesla forum report a vehicle aggressively avoiding random items in the road and reacting to a road repair site as if it was a pothole. Other forum users point out that early FSD updates often are a little shaky right at rollout but more polished by the time the release goes out more broadly.

Sources indicate that our own experience with Tesla’s FSD is that it works flawlessly—right up until it doesn’t and the driver needs to take over. Tesla’s own literature notes that drivers are expected to keep their attention on the road. The pretty latest graphics look attractive, but if you’re staring at the screen instead of out the windshield, FSD should theoretically automatically disconnect.

  • According to recent reports, the mod, known as OcarinaVR, was developed by ReTracedGames and builds upon the previously released PC port.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Less than three weeks after Nintendo launched its highly-anticipated The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on Nintendo Switch 2, PC customers are working hard to prove why they’re the master race by transforming the game entirely with an immersive new VR mode.

According to recent reports, the mod, known as OcarinaVR, was developed by ReTracedGames and builds upon the previously released PC port. It is showing the true skills of the PC modding community, and at what speed they can work to develop player experiences beyond a game’s original console boundaries.

The power of the OcarinaVR mod is quite the sight to behold. It goes beyond just being a camera trick, and instead shifts the entire game into a true first-person perspective with accurate spatial scaling—meaning the world adjusts depending on whether the player is controlling young Link or the grown-up version.

The mod also brings intricate control mechanics and hand tracking, allowing players to map and control Link’s arms and individual fingers using their VR controllers. Swinging the Master sword and bashing enemies with the Hylian shield never looks so satisfying and adds a sense of depth and realism to the game beyond just its graphics.

Industry observers note that ocarinaVR also manages UI elements and prevents clutter, displaying HUD readouts like heart count and the minimap as floating panels. Pre-rendered cutscenes are displayed on a curved virtual cinema screen for maximum immersion as the perspective shifts back to the 3rd person.

OcarinaVR … goes beyond just being a camera trick, and instead shifts the entire game into a true first-person perspective.

The mod is based on the Hookshot PC recompilation that was released on PC shortly after Ocarina of Time launched on Nintendo Switch 2 on November 5. That release already brought native widescreen and uncapped framerates, meaning it was a solid foundation for the OcarinaVR mod to build off.

Fan response to the Ocarina of Time remake has been monumental, with players praising its highly-detailed graphics and faithful retelling of the classic Zelda tale. Critics loved it equally as much, giving it one of the highest ratings on Metacritic of all time—a solid 95/100 aggregated score.

In DualShockers’ own review, Tayna Garcia wrote that the remake gives returning players an “opportunity to experience those same feelings again” from their childhoods, powered by nostalgia, but said it's a perfect place for newcomers to start their Zelda journey, too.

Fan response to the Ocarina of Time remake has been monumental [and] critics loved it equally as much.

The game was swiftly followed by Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto 6—perhaps the most hyped game of all time (and the highest reviewed on Metacritic with a stunning score of 99). Nintendo knew to get Zelda out the door before the news cycle and social media turned to GTA 6 for who knows how long.

The upcoming VR mod gives fans a chance to take on Ocarina of Time in a whole new way, snatching a little bit of attention back from the Vice City-drenched mediascape right now.
