Powerful fresh weight-loss drug helps patients cut knee pain in half

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1138 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For people living with painful knee osteoarthritis (OA), even simple activities like walking, climbing stairs, or getting out of a chair can become a struggle.
  • In a recent development, the two phase 3 trials, led by Northwestern University, included more than 1,000 participants in total.
  • The benefits extended beyond weight loss and improved knee pain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For people living with painful knee osteoarthritis (OA), even simple activities like walking, climbing stairs, or getting out of a chair can become a struggle. Excess body weight can make these challenges even worse. Now, two major clinical trials suggest that a powerful experimental weight-loss drug could provide substantial relief.

In a recent development, the two phase 3 trials, led by Northwestern University, included more than 1,000 participants in total. People receiving the highest dose of retatrutide, an experimental injectable weight-loss medication, lost an average of about 25% of their body weight. When researchers combined the findings from both trials, they found that approximately two-thirds of participants treated with retatrutide reported a reduction in knee pain of at least 50%. By comparison, only 38% of those given a placebo experienced that level of relief.

The benefits extended beyond weight loss and improved knee pain. Participants also indicated reductions in blood pressure, blood lipid levels, and inflammation throughout the body.

Findings from both studies were published on Nov. 8 in the Fresh England Journal of Medicine.

Recent findings suggest that "The findings are really saying for people who are overweight and have OA, if you lose a significant amount of weight with this treatment, there is a good chance that you're going to get a meaningful reduction in your knee pain," stated corresponding author Dr. Thomas Schnitzer, professor of physical medicine and rehabilitation, anesthesiology and medicine (rheumatology) at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine.

"A major factor is that you're loading your knees less and therefore, there's less pain and it allows you to increase your function.".

According to recent reports, philip Conaghan, a study co-author and professor of musculoskeletal medicine at the University of Leeds in the United Kingdom, presented results from one of the trials, TRIUMPH-4, on Nov. 8 at the American College of Rheumatology annual meeting in Orlando, Florida. Findings from the second trial, TRIUMPH-1-OA, were scheduled for presentation during a separate poster session that same day.

A Potential New Treatment for Millions With Knee Osteoarthritis.

Painful knee osteoarthritis affects approximately 5% of Americans (15 million people). Available treatments range from physical therapy and medications applied to the skin to oral anti-inflammatory drugs such as ibuprofen and Voltaren. Other options include opioids and corticosteroid injections, although the relief provided by steroid injections generally lasts only a short time.

Weight loss is another established way to ease symptoms. Previous studies have shown that losing 5% to 10% of body weight through changes in diet and exercise can improve knee osteoarthritis pain. However, Schnitzer explained that losing more than 10% through these approaches alone is often challenging. For people already struggling with painful knees, exercising enough to achieve substantial weight loss can be especially difficult.

According to recent reports, retatrutide could offer another approach. Developed by Eli Lilly, the experimental medication is administered as a once-weekly injection and works differently from existing GLP-1 medications such as semaglutide and tirzepatide.

While those drugs act on one or two hormone receptors and typically produce weight reductions of 10% to 20%, retatrutide activates receptors associated with three different naturally occurring hormones. In the clinical trials, participants lost approximately 20% to 25% of their body weight, depending on the dose. Eli Lilly scientists also contributed to the research as study co-authors.

"Participants had remarkable responses," Schnitzer noted. "Many of the people in this study lost considerable amounts of weight, with a few losing up to a hundred pounds or more.".

Why Diet and Exercise Still Matter.

Despite the encouraging findings, Schnitzer emphasized that lifestyle changes should remain the starting point for people who are overweight and have painful knee osteoarthritis.

According to recent reports, improving eating habits, increasing physical activity, and making other sustainable lifestyle adjustments can help reduce symptoms without the expense of newer weight-loss medications. These strategies also avoid side effects associated with GLP-1 drugs, including gastrointestinal problems and muscle loss.

Maintaining muscle strength is particularly vital for people with knee osteoarthritis because the muscles surrounding the joint help support and stabilize it. Losing too much muscle could therefore create additional challenges for patients who already have difficulty moving comfortably.

For individuals who cannot achieve sufficient weight loss through lifestyle changes and continue to experience significant knee pain, Schnitzer believes retatrutide could become a valuable option if it receives approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

Could the Drug Also Slow Knee Arthritis Progression?

Although the trials demonstrated substantial improvements in weight and pain, several important questions remain unanswered.

According to recent reports, one of the biggest is whether retatrutide does more than relieve symptoms. Researchers still do not know if the drug can slow the underlying progression of knee osteoarthritis enough to reduce the likelihood that patients will eventually need knee replacement surgery. People who already required a knee replacement were excluded from the trials.

"That would be the goal here to say you can reduce people's pain, and you can stop the progression of their osteoarthritis," Schnitzer noted.

According to recent reports, another unanswered question is whether retatrutide might benefit people with painful knee osteoarthritis who are not overweight. Because the trials did not include these patients, further studies will be needed to determine whether they could experience similar improvements.

Researchers are also interested in understanding how much of the pain relief comes directly from weight loss and how much might be related to the drug's effects on inflammation.

According to recent reports, "These drugs are believed to have significant anti-inflammatory activity, but the mechanism is not entirely known," Schnitzer said. "Whether cutting down inflammation in the joint is also important in addition to reducing load needs more research, so this is still a first step, in my view. I've been working in the OA field for a long time, and I think this opens up opportunities to do a lot more studies to understand the condition better.".

How Researchers Measured Knee Pain Relief.

To evaluate changes in symptoms, the research teams used the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Arthritis Index (WOMAC) Pain index, a standardized tool for assessing osteoarthritis pain.

Sources indicate that during study visits, participants rated their pain on a scale from 0 to 10. They also used a mobile app to record their pain levels each day, allowing researchers to track how symptoms changed throughout treatment.

The study is titled, "Retatrutide Once Weekly in Adults with Knee Osteoarthritis Pain and Obesity.".

Materials provided by Northwestern University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

Zenless Zone Zero's big end-of-year revision brings multiplayer combat, free Zhao, and the first dual-form Agent

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program has delivered the good news on Version 2.5, To Be Fuel for the Night.
  • To start with, Version 2.5 arrives on December 30, making it the game’s last major enhancement of the year, which also means players are in for some freebies to celebrate the fresh year.
  • Recent findings suggest that of course, the biggest addition in Version 2.5 is Ye Shunguang, the game’s fresh Agent, who’s a Void Hunter, and also Zenless Zone Zero’s first dual-form Agent.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program has delivered the good news on Version 2.5, To Be Fuel for the Night. This chapter is a massive deal for a few reasons, not least of which because it brings an end to Season 2.

To start with, Version 2.5 arrives on December 30, making it the game’s last major enhancement of the year, which also means players are in for some freebies to celebrate the fresh year.

Recent findings suggest that of course, the biggest addition in Version 2.5 is Ye Shunguang, the game’s fresh Agent, who’s a Void Hunter, and also Zenless Zone Zero’s first dual-form Agent. Zhao also becomes a playable Agent as part of this update - two things HoYoverse teased last week at The Game Awards.

Recent findings suggest that ye Shunguang’s unique attribute is Honed Edge, through which she can enter an Enlightened Mind state. Ye Shunguang’s signature Ether Veil can deliver Honed Edge damage as she applies a vulnerability effect to enemies. She arrives alongside her sidekick, Bangboo Sprout, who keeps with her swordplay theme by calling down flying swords.

According to recent reports, zhao is the other playable Agent as mentioned, an S-Rank Ice Defence legend. Zhao is a fast and nimble attacker who uses her giant greataxe to suppress enemies. Zhao can trigger Ether Veil: Wellspring by using Frostbite she accumulates, which buffs the entire squad.

According to recent reports, narratively, this particular chapter will reveal the fate of Waifei Peninsula. The quest is gonna take the squad deeper into the Lumite Mine ruins, and the newly introduced Perception Technique is how you’ll uncover the answers hidden within.

According to recent reports, there’s a gameplay component to that, too. Ye Shunguang's Bladeflash Mirage ability will come in handy during the story’s big investigation, which comes with unique rewards, including a fresh W-Engine.

Version 2.5 is also the one set to give players the first taste of multiplayer combat thought he limited-time Joint Investigation: The Divine Maze event. As part of that, you can have three-Agent squads face off against each other in unique combat challenges.

Industry observers note that there’s even more to get excited about in this one. Proxy Outpost lets you create your own Outposts, and join those created by other. This is more of a social feature than anything, though.

HoYoverse is also making a series of updates to Soldier 11, Grace, Soldier 0 – Anby, Ellen, and Burnice, all of whom will see their mechanics updated and their effectiveness boosted. Similar updates are on the way for other Agents, which will arrive in future updates. Shiyu Defense and Deadly Assault has seen some adjustments to the gameplay loop, too.

According to recent reports, finally, HoYoverse is making it easier for players to jump into 2.5’s latest story chapter using Advance Screening. Ye Shunguang and Zhao will be available for the entire revision’s duration, and reruns in the second half will guarantee another S-Rank.

According to recent reports, you’ll be able to pick from Alice, Soldier 0 – Anby, or Astra. Zhao will herself be available as a login bonus alongside 1,000 Polychromes, a upcoming outfit for Jane, and more. If you’re looking to jump in on December 30, don’t do so without having a look at our Zenless Zone Zero codes page to get some freebies.

The best soft launch mobile games for iPhone, iPad or Android

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The biggest games yet to launch on the global market.
  • If you've been looking for something newly introduced and exciting that isn't quite fully released, then look no further; you've found our list of the best games at the moment in soft launch.
  • In a recent development, sometimes developers like to make sure the paying public is willing to play their game before they push it to every device in the world - that's where soft launch comes in.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The biggest games yet to launch on the global market.

If you've been looking for something newly introduced and exciting that isn't quite fully released, then look no further; you've found our list of the best games at the moment in soft launch.

In a recent development, sometimes developers like to make sure the paying public is willing to play their game before they push it to every device in the world - that's where soft launch comes in. Available in just a handful of countries and regions, a soft-launched game is subject to drastic change as developers take on board customer feedback (and other metrics) to alter the game and ensure the best possible product is ready for when it goes to worldwide launch.

In a recent development, but here's the kicker - we can see when developers do that. And when you're looking at some of the substantial games, like the ones we have on this list, then you can find yourself getting very excited, and even a little jealous that you can't play them yet.

So to help you out a little, we've collected a huge list of some of the biggest and best games at the moment available in soft launch, which you might well be able to get if you have the right Apple ID or Google Play account to download them with.

Just as a note: In the case of a game suddenly disappearing, it might be because the developer has decided to stop development on it early and save themselves the cost of a massive launch, or because the developer is gearing up for a big launch and wants to surprise the world. Whatever the case, we'll try to keep you updated when these things happen.

Let's get into the list! SoulTerra Odyssey.

An interesting one here. Bandai Namco has dived back into the mobile world with a completely new IP. They're also claiming it's the first 'Match3D Roguelite Battle Game ever.' Given the sheer breadth of games out there, I highly doubt it, but it's an intriguing combination, nonetheless.

Sonic Rumble sees the blue blur returning to mobile, this time as a battle royale of sorts. In the mould of games like Stumble Guys and Fall Guys, it appears we can expect to dash around obstacle-filled courses, dodging the numerous hazards that threaten to eliminate us at every turn. It's definitely a setup that suits Sonic and co, but is it entering a market that's already been conquered by Scopely? Only time will tell.

Casual strategy games are all the rage these days, particularly on mobile. Anything that gives you a slight hit of feeling clever without requiring in-depth tactics that take forever to learn. Century Games' Crown of Bones is the latest attempt at sliding into that niche. It sees you joining the Skeleton King and his army as they battle through numerous realms. It sports a colourful art style that reminds me somewhat of little toy towns and villages, something you might have created in real life as a child, perhaps. As for the gameplay, it pretty much consists of increasing your numbers, upgrading your troops and toppling your opponents. There are a few special items thrown in for good measure as well.

It has been revealed that if you're a football fan, you're probably already aware of Nordeus as the folks behind the popular management sim Top Eleven. With their latest effort, Top Goal, they are swapping the touchline for the pitch as you take direct control over your squad, having a more active role in the outcome of a match. Still, it seems some of the strategic side remains as you build your squad and choose your formation before taking on other players in PvP.

Industry observers note that while it might seem as though the era of endless runners has passed on mobile, several still do very well, particularly if they have brand power behind them. Zapak hopes that Ben 10 Alien Run can join that list, putting a lot of stock in the popular children's cartoon pulling in the younger generation.

In it, you will dash around while transforming into one of nine different aliens, each bringing special abilities to the table. That might be creating a shield to block an enemy attack in one instance, while another might clear the path ahead with laser beams. On top of that, there are the usual daily challenges and missions you'd expect from the genre.

According to recent reports, oh My Anne is a match-3 game based on the popular novel series Anne of Green Gables. Players proceed through the story by completing levels and associated challenges. It's certainly interesting to see Neowiz deciding to take established, historical (1908~) novels and their IP and spin them off into games. There's a question to be asked about brand recognition and 'crossover IP' when those IPs are not ones from the current vogue. We regularly see Warhammer and Marvel crossover games, but those things are at the moment 'in', Anne of Green Gables — and Oh My Anne — targets a different audience and plays by different rules of advertising. Could there be a Dracula, Canterbury Tales or Beowulf games on the horizon if this takes off?

In a recent development, netEase's Stumble Guys killer, Eggy Party, is rapidly moving toward its global release with seven fresh regions granted access to it in January of 2024; before that, it was simply in the SEA region. What's the big appeal? Well, if you're not sold by the constant party, cheerful colours and multiplayer mania of Eggy Party, then maybe the map creation will be the thing to grab your attention. A bumbling race to the finish might be fun, but doing it on a map that you - or one of your friends - created is vastly more fun.

It has been revealed that zynga, who you likely know for, well, many things, are working on a upcoming addition to their growing merge catalogue. FruitFall – don't forget the double capital Fs – tasks you with merging fruits to beat each level. Simple, right? Judging by the store description, expect this to become more difficult as you progress. At first, it'll likely be a case of simply merging fruit, while the latter stages will introduce troublesome crates and frozen fruit that need thawing out before becoming useful. Zynga claims each level brings something different, keeping the challenge fresh and fun. Time will tell if that's the case.

Mattel Match: Toybox looks to bring together the company's many toys under one roof, including Uno, Masters of the Universe and, of course, Barbie. How? You might ask. Through match-3 puzzling, that's how.

Recent findings suggest that as you'll likely have guessed from the name, Puzzletown Mysteries sees you unravel mysteries by solving puzzles. There is also a town involved. The overarching whodunit is whether poor Gladys slipped from her balcony or if she received a little push before toppling over the edge, while you'll also look into a case of stolen cats.

Industry observers note that as you've likely already guessed from the name, we're talking tower defence here. Here, the slight twist on the usual formula is that, alongside setting up your various defences, you'll actually build the map your enemies will march down. Of course, that's something we've seen before, but it's a fun twist nevertheless. I'm quite fond of the visuals, which have a super clean and easy-to-read look that's just shy of qualifying as minimalist.

Recent findings suggest that diamond Dreams is looking to bring a sense of elegance to the match-3 genre. The whole idea is that you're working towards crafting some stunning jewellery that, I have to say, looks far better than it possibly needs to.

In a recent development, given the immense popularity of Monopoly Go, it seemed inevitable that similar games would pop up eventually. Coin Master – Board Adventure from Moon Active is one such attempt. Having already achieved success with Coin Master, I'd imagine this will also do incredibly well.

Cats & Soup has made a name for itself in recent times with its lovely aesthetic and focus on feline companions. While it's still a fairly familiar idle RPG, the focus on cosiness helped it stand out from a massive crowd. Evidently buoyed by its success, a spin-off called Cats & Soup: Magic Recipe is now in the works. Once again, the team are taking on a familiar mobile genre, bringing some warm-fuzzy cuteness to the merge-and-match realm. The aim is to cook delicious recipes, build a lovely home for your kitties, and make friends with newly introduced cats.

Sources indicate that the humble match-3 will likely never lose popularity on mobile. It's simple to understand and great for playing on the go since it hits a nice spot between relaxing and engaging the brain. It's not surprising, then, that we often have big franchises delve into the genre. The latest to try their white-gloved hand is Disney with Disney Magic Match 3D. In it, you'll remove colourful clutter. No, really. Check out Catherine's preview to learn more.

Sources indicate that while George R R Martin might have no interest in finishing his own book series, there is still plenty of Game of Thrones content to enjoy. Dragonfire is the latest, a tile-based strategy game that lets you put the titular fire-breathing winged beasties to work. But it's not simply sending them into battle. You will hatch and train them, taking your little fiery friend from a cute baby to a creature capable of barbecuing enemy villages.

In a recent development, we all love Fruit Ninja, but if there's one criticism you can throw its way, it's that it didn't have much else going for it beyond slicing up fruit. Adventure looks to change this by introducing a level-based approach that sees you solving puzzles alongside stabbing melons. You can also unlock upcoming weapons and abilities as you progress, presumably allowing you to dice a kiwi in untold ways.

FairyTale Quest is a roguelite action RPG in the style of something like Vampire Survivors. And its characters? Well, as you've likely guessed, they're all pulled from traditional stories. So you can expect the Big Bad Wolf and Red Riding Hood to fight by your side. They can put aside their differences for the greater good, it seems.

In a recent development, that's right. Plants Vs Zombies 3 is back in soft launch, this time with Evolved after the colon. This refers to the merging mechanics they're throwing in with their latest attempt. We'll see how that all pans out in due course, but it's hard not to be a little sceptical given that EA has clearly struggled to figure out what they want to do with PvZ.

According to recent reports, it's been almost ten years since Hill Climb Racing 2 launched, so it likely feels about time for a sequel for fans of wacky, physics-based driving. In the third instalment, you can expect plenty of special gadgets and handy boosts for increasing your performance on the bouncy track. There are also the plentiful customisation options on offer that any self-respecting racer needs. If we can't pimp our ride, what's the point?

Sources indicate that aside from the obvious flock and little green candy-loving monster, there are few games more iconic on mobile than Temple Run. That's why the announcement of a third has got us excited here at Pocket Gamer. But do those simple yet effective mechanics stand up after all these years, or are massive changes needed? Well, check out Catherine's Temple Run 3 preview to see what she thought.

Recent findings suggest that cute little penguins running around an obstacle course in Fall/Stumble Guys fashion? Haven't we already seen this with Pudgy Party? Apparently, Smilegate thinks they can do better, and personally, I'm all for it. Penguins are wonderful little creatures, and the more games where they're the star, the better. It sees you participating in 10-minute matches where the aim is to get your beak across the line first.

Sources indicate that if you love pinging marbles and cutesy creatures, Marblebound might be the perfect fit for you. You gather a team of four heroes and then head into battle to take down a series of fearsome foes. And you'll do that by firing marbles at them, including ricocheting them off walls if you know your angles.

According to recent reports, funPlus, who you may know from State of Survival and DC: Dark Legion, among others, appears to be working on a new game. This one's called Dark Shot Survival and sees you building up a base to fend off night creatures (yes, they look like zombies to me, too). The whole thing seems to centre around a day/night cycle, wherein you spend the waking hours gathering resources and fortifying your base. Then, when the sun goes down, you'll need to fend off the zomb— sorry, night creatures, with all your might.

In a recent development, angry Birds Rush sees Rovio's recognisable avians slinging themselves into a different genre. By the looks of things, Rush is an endless runner that sees you bouncing through various colourful locales all inspired by the series' many other games. It doesn't appear to be a straightforward runner, though, with slingshot elements still present to some extent.

There are few cartoon duos more iconic than Tom & Jerry. I'm not even a huge fan of them, but they'd certainly spring to mind if I had to name two long-standing cartoon rivals. It's that instant recognition that probably helped Steer Studios decide it was an IP worth working with. Tom and Jerry Blast is a puzzler that, based on the screenshots, sees you tapping your way through each level and using boosters if they ever become overly tricky.

Industry observers note that you wouldn't necessarily put sailing the seven seas and tower defence together, but that's exactly what Puzala is going for with Stormborn Era. In it, you take charge of Black Sam and his crew, defending their ship from the hordes of enemies that have nothing better to do with their time than attack a big boat.

The Girls' Frontline series has proven incredibly popular over the years. Apparently, conventionally attractive women with guns will always do well. Who knew? Anyway, you can check out Catherine's Ahead of the Game to see if it's more than just a surface-level shooter.

It has been revealed that having briefly appeared in the US a while back, Borderlands Mobile has crept back into soft launch in Canada. The latest iteration has revealed that we can play as long-time fan-favourite Mad Moxxi, which I'm sure will be welcome news to many folks.

It has been revealed that update [Sat 21st Nov 2026, 6pm]: Although this story started as a win for the Ocarina remake, it's taken a rather unexpected turn. As our colleagues at Push Square report, fans of GTA 6 are now allegedly going after Zelda's user scores on Metacritic.

Push Square: "In response to a coordinated review bombing effort on GTA 6, fans of the Rockstar release appear to have rolled out a counter-attack on The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, believing Nintendo gamers are to blame for the situation...The Switch 2’s universally adored remake of Ocarina of Time has seen its user score drop from 9.6 to 8.9 at the time of writing.".

Zelda has retained a user score of 9.6/10 on Metacritic since its launch earlier this month, but as mentioned above, it's now dropped. At the time of publishing this enhancement, it still has a "positive" rating after more than 32,000 user reviews.

As we noted in our original story, there can be all sorts of factors in play when it comes to Metacritic user scores, and they're subject to change over time (and can bounce back).

Original Story: It's been a huge year for the games industry with all sorts of heavy-hitters releasing over the past few months, and as we look towards the end of 2026, we're now checking in on Metacritic's highest-rated games of the year based on the user score.

While Grand Theft Auto 6 may have officially surpassed Ocarina's Remake as the highest-rated game of 2026 on the review aggregate website (and also matched the original N64 hit as the highest-rated critic Metascore of all time), it seems the classic outing on Switch 2 has won players' hearts worldwide.

Industry observers note that according to the latest update from the site, Ocarina's Remake is at the moment sitting in the top highest-rated games (above 90), based on user score. It's in good company with other games like Resident Evil Requiem and Splatoon Raiders.

It has been revealed that obviously, there are all sorts of different factors in play here when it comes to user scores (and the system in place isn't necessarily perfect). For example, Ocarina's Remake has over 25,000 user reviews, whereas other titles may have around 100 reviews. Keep in mind, user scores are also subject to change over time.

And if you're wondering how GTA 6 has been received by players, it's currently sitting on a user score of 5.5/10 after more than 30,000 user reviews. Even with supposed review bombings, it might take some time before it wins over some players. Despite top marks from critics, this upcoming entry in the GTA universe appears to have divided the fanbase in its opening week.

As attention shifts towards the end-of-year game awards, both Ocarina and GTA 6 have already been nominated for multiple industry awards.

This simple habit is linked to a 33% lower risk of Alzheimer's

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that reading for enjoyment may offer far more than entertainment.
  • In a recent development, researchers at the University of Cambridge are working with The Queen's Reading Room, a charity established by Her Majesty The Queen, to raise awareness of these benefits across all age groups.
  • Cambridge psychiatry researchers Professor Barbara Sahakian and Dr.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that reading for enjoyment may offer far more than entertainment. Whether someone prefers a classic Jane Austen novel or a Heartstopper graphic novel, research suggests that reading for pleasure is associated with better mental health, stronger empathy, and a lower risk of dementia.

In a recent development, researchers at the University of Cambridge are working with The Queen's Reading Room, a charity established by Her Majesty The Queen, to raise awareness of these benefits across all age groups. Their collaboration is part of the National Year of Reading, an initiative encouraging more people to make reading part of their lives.

Cambridge psychiatry researchers Professor Barbara Sahakian and Dr. Christelle Langley began exploring the subject while writing their 2025 book, Brain Boost: Healthy Habits for a Happier Life. They discovered that reading for enjoyment was connected to a remarkably wide range of positive outcomes, yet the amount of research specifically examining these benefits was surprisingly limited.

Industry observers note that in a review published in Psychological Medicine, Sahakian and Langley joined Vicki Perrin, CEO of The Queen's Reading Room, to examine the available evidence. Their findings suggest that the format and type of reading matter less than the enjoyment people get from it. They also highlight how reading together, whether through book clubs or parents sharing stories with children, can provide additional benefits.

Recent findings suggest that professor Sahakian said: "Reading is a great way to support our brain health, develop important cognitive skills and boost our well-being. It's something we ought to be encouraging from an early age, given the increasing evidence of its benefits, particularly to children, but really, it's never too late to start, and it can bring benefits throughout our lives and into old age.".

Reading Early in Life Is Linked to Better Brain Development.

Despite the growing evidence of its advantages, reading for enjoyment has become less common among young people. Surveys indicate that reading rates among children and teenagers have fallen to their lowest recorded levels, with particularly steep challenges among teenage boys and children from disadvantaged backgrounds.

Even children who are least enthusiastic about reading recognize that it can help them academically. Nearly half acknowledge that books and other reading materials can introduce them to unfamiliar words or teach them something latest.

It has been revealed that one of the most compelling studies examined more than 10,000 young people. Conducted by Sahakian, Langley, and their colleagues, the research found that children who started reading for pleasure at an early age tended to perform better in several key areas. These included attention, memory, and executive functioning, the mental abilities involved in planning, decision-making, and managing behavior.

In a recent development, early readers also highlighted stronger academic performance, experienced fewer mental health problems, and were more likely to develop healthier daily routines. In particular, they tended to get more sleep and spend less time using screens.

Dr. Langley stated: "Given how beneficial reading for pleasure is at a young age, we should be doing everything we can to introduce children and young people to reading. The key thing is to find something they'd really enjoy reading about - it might be a TV program or a game - and use this as a way in. Reading comics and graphic novels could also be a helpful introduction as they might be seen as less intimidating, maybe less boring, than novels.".

The academic advantages may extend beyond language and literacy. Studies have also connected reading with stronger mathematical performance. Researchers suggest this relationship may arise because both activities rely on some of the same mental abilities, including language processing, memory, and executive function.

Just Five Minutes of Reading May Reduce Stress.

Sources indicate that the benefits of reading do not disappear after childhood. Among adults, surveys have associated reading for enjoyment with improved emotional well-being, greater relaxation, and reduced stress. Readers also tend to report more empathy, a deeper understanding of other people, and greater openness to viewpoints different from their own.

It has been revealed that for many people, books are an especially appealing way to unwind. Reading ranks as the most popular approach to stress relief, with nearly two in five adults (38%) identifying it as their preferred way to relax.

A neuroscience study commissioned by The Queen's Reading Room in 2024 found that spending just five minutes reading fiction could lower stress by as much as 20%. The study also reported improvements in concentration and problem-solving abilities, along with a reduced sense of loneliness.

Books may even provide more comfort than some traditional relaxation habits. In one survey, more respondents noted they turned to reading (35%) for comfort than to drinking wine (31%) or taking a hot bath (10%).

Reading Linked to Lower Dementia and Alzheimer's Risk.

As people get older, the potential advantages of reading may become especially meaningful. Research has associated mentally stimulating leisure activities, including reading, with slower cognitive decline and a reduced likelihood of developing dementia.

One study followed nearly 5,500 adults aged 55 and older for five years. Participants who regularly took part in activities such as reading were significantly less likely to develop cognitive impairment during the study period.

Another investigation reported an even more striking association. People who read newspapers, magazines, and books had a 33% lower risk of Alzheimer's disease.

These findings suggest that keeping the mind engaged through reading may support cognitive health in later life. However, the researchers emphasize that most of the available studies identify associations rather than proving that reading itself prevents dementia.

How Reading May Change the Structure of the Brain.

What could explain the many benefits associated with reading? Brain imaging research offers some intriguing clues.

In a recent development, studies have identified differences in brain structure associated with reading, particularly in regions responsible for language, learning, emotional regulation, and executive control. These differences include greater brain volume and larger cortical areas in certain regions, as well as thicker cortex in areas important for language processing.

Researchers have also observed stronger connections within the brain's white matter, which helps different regions communicate and supports the processing of language.

Although much of this evidence is correlational, some research suggests that reading-related training can directly influence the brain's physical structure.

Recent findings suggest that in one small study involving 11 children with dyslexia between the ages of 7 and 11, researchers tested an eight-week training program designed to strengthen reading abilities. The exercises involved mental imagery, articulation, and tracing letters, combinations of letters, and words.

Following the program, the children demonstrated significant improvements in reading skills. Brain scans also revealed increases in gray matter volume in notable regions, providing evidence that reading interventions can be accompanied by measurable structural changes in the brain.

Why Reading Together May Offer Even Greater Benefits.

Reading does not have to be a solitary activity. Researchers suggest that sharing books with other people can add a valuable social dimension, creating opportunities for connection and potentially improving both mental and physical well-being.

According to recent reports, the Queen's Reading Room has made this idea a central part of its mission. Launched on social media in January 2021, the initiative originally provided a way for people to exchange book recommendations and stay connected during pandemic lockdowns.

It has since expanded into an international community reaching more than 12 million people across 184 countries. Through its flagship festival, neuroscience research, and other programs, the charity works to make reading a more prominent part of everyday life.

Its activities also extend to homeless shelters and domestic violence refuges, where shared reading is used as a therapeutic resource to help people during recovery.

The social connections created through reading groups may be particularly valuable for older adults, who can face increased isolation and reduced opportunities to participate in physically demanding activities.

It has been revealed that professor Sahakian remarked: "Shared reading groups and book clubs appear to provide additional benefits through social interaction. They can help people feel less isolated and more connected to others, which has been shown to reduce the risk of dementia.

"While these clubs can be fun and beneficial at any age, they're perfect for older people who may not be so mobile - they might not be able to go out as an exercise group or a cycling group, but a reading group is something most people can enjoy.".

The researchers' overall message is that people can benefit from reading at any stage of life. Whether someone enjoys novels, newspapers, comics, or stories shared with friends, making time for reading may help support cognitive health, emotional well-being, and social connection.

Sources indicate that vicki Perrin, CEO of The Queen's Reading Room, added: "At The Queen's Reading Room, we have seen first-hand the transformative power of individual and shared reading to change lives. Books truly do make life better, and we're excited to do our bit to help everyone, everywhere, make more room for reading.".

8 Best Connections to GTA 5 in GTA 6

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that rockstar spent a long time working on Grand Theft Auto 6, and it highlights through the games many small details.
  • Sources indicate that more specifically, there are a decent number that connect back to GTA 5.
  • Recent findings suggest that thanks to GTA 6, we now the answers to these questions, and there are many more connections to GTA 5 that you might not have discovered.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that rockstar spent a long time working on Grand Theft Auto 6, and it highlights through the games many small details. There are tons of hidden easter eggs and secrets scattered across Leonida, and some of them connect to previous GTA titles.

Sources indicate that more specifically, there are a decent number that connect back to GTA 5. Have you ever wondered what happened to Michael’s boat? Who took the blame for the murder of Floyd and Debora?

Recent findings suggest that thanks to GTA 6, we now the answers to these questions, and there are many more connections to GTA 5 that you might not have discovered. Everything is connected after all.

If you played GTA 5, odds are you spent a great deal of time exploring the map and going from town to town. It was quite a big map, but you wouldn’t have spent your entire time in the city, so you probably recognize Grapeseed and the Grand Senora Desert.

Grapeseed is a small town in the northern part of the GTA 5 map, with it residing in Blaine County. The Grand Senora Desert is a much larger area, but it also resides in Blaine County.

While exploring the many buildings that you can enter in GTA 6, you can wander into a few trailers, and some of them have postcards that link Leonida to Los Santos. You can find postcards specifically for Grapeseed and Grand Senora Desert.

In a recent development, you get a lot of phone calls in GTA 5. Many missions start with you getting a call, and then proceeding to head to some location. Because of this, if you have played the story, you will have heard Michael’s ringtone quite a bit.

Sources indicate that well, if you feel so inclined, and want to stay true to the spirit of GTA 5, you can have Michael’s ringtone in GTA 6. All you need to do is go into your phone’s settings, choose the ringtone option, and then select the one called Wind Chimes.

This ringtone is exactly the same as Michael’s from GTA 5, giving you that classic GTA feeling from 13 years ago when you played the campaign for GTA 5.

One of the best easter eggs in GTA 6 is that you can find Michael’s boat from GTA 5, and you don’t really need to go all that far. In fact, you have to stick rather close to home, because it is sitting right outside Jason’s house at the start of the game.

In a recent development, michael ends up having his boat stolen in GTA 5, and you never learn what happens to it. Well, it somehow found its way to Leonida and ended up in Jason’s yard.

If you decide to climb up on the boat, you can see that a screen is still active on it. This screen shows the shores of Los Santos from GTA 5, seemingly proving that this is indeed the same boat that was stolen from Michael all those years ago.

According to recent reports, do you remember Fabien? He teaches Michael how to do yoga in GTA 5, and is known for having some rather… suggestive yoga poses. Throughout GTA 5, you can perform yoga as Michael either at his house or at the peak of Mount Gordo.

In a recent development, fabien has been doing well since the events of GTA 5, and you can see what he has been up to thanks to his article in one of the game’s magazines. This is also an easter egg that you can find outside of Jason’s house.

Go out onto the porch, and open the magazine that is on the table near the workout equipment. Flip through the pages, and you will find that Fabien has been doing well. He has been on an “epic pilgrimage of enlightenment.”.

It has been revealed that it is a little ambiguous as to if the Mount Chiliad Mystery in GTA 5 was ever solved. While there is a means of seeing a UFO from it, it didn’t have a narrative conclusion, so it is debated on whether or not it was ever completed.

In a recent development, however, this mystery is mentioned in GTA 6, and it is on a vehicle. You can find an RV in Leonida that is covered in phrases like, “Don’t be fooled,” and “There’s no driving away.”.

Recent findings suggest that what connects this to Mount Chiliad is the eye symbol. It is the same eye symbol that is found at the top of the Mount Chiliad mural, making it seem like the mystery was never fully solved, or maybe that is just what Rockstar wants us to think.

According to recent reports, there are some small nods to GTA 5 hidden throughout GTA 6, and one that is easy to overlook is a small book review for a novel sitting in Jason’s house. The book in question is titled Lethal By Design: A Liberty City Memoir, written by Tom Everett.

In a recent development, this book connects to the events of GTA 4 and Niko Bellic - a fan-favorite protagonist. With that being said, one of the reviews is actually from a resident of Los Santos.

The review reads, “Illuminating, revelatory, heartbreaking, and pulse-quickening - and that’s before you’ve even finished the editor’s forward.” This review came from Alison Taylor from the Los Santos Book Review.

There is an obscure reference to GTA 5 in GTA 6, and it connects back to some of the promotional material for GTA 5. One of the trailers for GTA 5 featured a man with a newspaper on his desk.

According to recent reports, if you are paying attention, you can see that the newspaper’s headline reads, “Aliens ate my prize [blank]. Of course, I have to bleep out the final word due to vulgarity, but it connected to GTA 4, and it also played into the insane satirical nature of GTA 5.

This same newspaper has returned, and it is in GTA 6. In a shack in the Grassrivers, you can spot the same newspaper sitting on a table. It is amazing that Rockstar remembered to bring back this strange newspaper.

Floyd and Debora Hebert were an unhappy couple living in Vespucci Beach in GTA 5. Their house is used as a safehouse by Trevor and their cousin Wade. However, they don’t survive the events of GTA 5, as Trevor murders them in a brutal off-screen killing that leaves him covered in blood.

It is never known exactly what happened after that event, but you can learn the truth of what transpired after the events of GTA 5 by listening to the radio in GTA 6.

Sources indicate that if you listen to the crime thriller podcast channel on the radio, you will hear them talk about Floyd and Debora. It turns out that Wade got blamed for their deaths.

EA Sports has revealed 3 new Heroes coming to FC 26 Ultimate Team as part of Team 1 of the Winter Wildcards promo: Ivan Zamorano, Claudio Pizarro and Jill Scott.

The Bayern and Werder Bremen legend Claudio Pizarro is famously the Bundesliga’s oldest ever player, after turning out well past 40 years of age - up front no less. But he’s making an appearance in FC 26 because he won the Hero Vote Poll a few months ago, with the Peruvian edging out notable nutter Steffan Effenberg and the prolific Brazilian striker, Elber.

The love for South American Heroes continues with Ivan Zamorano presented in his Real Madrid guise rather than part of the unbelievably stacked Inter squad which featured legends and Icons ranging from current Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone to Javier Zanetti and Ronaldo Nazario.

And probably most interestingly, Queen of the Jungle and centurion Lioness, Jill Scott, is also coming to shore up the midfield with a card which fits the “Gullit Gang” pre-requisite of all face stats over 80 - including a dominant 91 physical befitting her role as one of the most recognisable enforcers in women’s football.

Whether her in-game body type will actually let her put that strength out on the pitch (she will surely also have Bruiser) remains to be seen, but she could easily have the gangly aura of Patrick Vieira if the rest of her PlayStyles are right.

Latest Ultimate Team Heroes have been added mid-season before, including the likes of Enzo Francescoli in FC 24, but 3 at once looks to indicate that EA is leaning on Heroes to add fan-favourite players to the game with a lower threshold than Icons.

Plus they can be given away for free without upsetting the power curve as much as Icons, as shown by the free Classic XI Heroes handed out recently (I got Mario Gomez, F).

The rest of the Winter Wildcards team features a host of equally famous, and now infamous, players with some featuring 99 stats and alternative positions.

Highlights include striker and CAM versions of Balon D’or holder Ousmane Dembele, but also everyone’s love-to-hate Low Driven Shot master, Claudia Pina.

There are also incredibly strong-looking Gabriel and Fede Valverde cards, as well as downgraded, and therefore hopefully cheaper, versions of Icons like Johan Cruyff.
